    roi="217/076", start_date="2015-01-01", end_date="2024-12-31",
    out_dir="./gee_stm", composite_type="stm",
    indices=["NDVI", "NBR"], metrics=["median", "p10", "p90", "iqr"],
    project="my-gcp-project",
)

Masked pixels are written as -inf (float outputs), the files' NoData value: load_raster reads them as NaN, which LandTrendr treats as a missing year. See the worked example.

docs.title: download_gee_image
docs.text:
zeit.gee.downloader.download_gee_image(
    image, roi, out_filename, method="auto", scale=30, tile_size=None,
    sub_tile_workers=16, crs="EPSG:4326", max_tile_mb=None,
    max_direct_mb=4096, max_retries=5, base_backoff=5.0,
)

Downloads one ee.Image to a local GeoTIFF by the fastest route that works. This is what download_gee_timeseries calls for each composite; use it directly for images you build yourself or to tune the download. The direct route fixes one pixel grid for the whole ROI and fetches it as tiles with concurrent ee.data.computePixels calls, writing each tile into its window of the output file (no temporary tiles, no mosaicking). Concurrency adapts to HTTP 429 responses.

Parameter Type Default Description image ee.Image required The image to download. roi ee.Geometry required Region whose bounding box is downloaded. Build it with resolve_roi. out_filename str required Output GeoTIFF. Never left partially written. method str "auto" "auto", "direct" or "drive". scale float 30 Pixel size in metres (converted to degrees at the equator for a geographic CRS, as Earth Engine does). tile_size float None Deprecated and ignored. sub_tile_workers int 16 Upper bound on concurrent requests. Starts at 4 and adapts to the account's limit (about 40 on a standard tier, about 2 in Restricted Mode). crs str "EPSG:4326" Output CRS, e.g. "EPSG:32723". max_tile_mb float None Cap on one tile request, in MB (at most 32, the default). max_direct_mb float 4096 With "auto", larger images (raw size) go to a Drive export. max_retries, base_backoff 5, 5.0 Retry policy for network or server errors. Throttled requests get short jittered retries instead.

Returns the output path, or None if the download failed (nothing is written in that case).

from zeit.gee.auth import initialize_gee
from zeit.gee.roi import resolve_roi
from zeit.gee.harmonization import get_harmonized_collection
from zeit.gee.composites import create_annual_medoid
from zeit.gee.downloader import download_gee_image

initialize_gee(project="my-gcp-project")
roi = resolve_roi("data/study_area.gpkg")       # or "217/076", "23KPQ", a bbox ...
col = get_harmonized_collection(roi, "1985-01-01", "2025-12-31")

for year in range(1985, 2026):
    img = create_annual_medoid(col, year)
    img = img.normalizedDifference(["SR_B5", "SR_B7"]).rename("NBR").toFloat()
    download_gee_image(img, roi, f"nbr_{year}.tif", crs="EPSG:32723", sub_tile_workers=32)

initialize_gee(project=None, *, key_file=None) uses the credentials earthengine authenticate saved, and asks to authenticate when there are none, in a terminal or a notebook. In a batch job, with no one to answer, it raises a RuntimeError that says what to do instead of waiting: authenticate once on the login node (the credentials go to ~/.config/earthengine, which compute nodes usually see), or use a service account, whose JSON key key_file or the variable GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS names (its project is the default project). Without internet access it says so, and that zeit fetch tiles builds the tiles of gee_tiles beforehand.

docs.title: resolve_roi
docs.text:
zeit.gee.roi.resolve_roi(roi)

Turns any supported area description into the ee.Geometry the Earth Engine functions need, so your code never builds Earth Engine objects. Local inputs are reduced to their bounding box.

Parameter Type Default Description roi see below required Area description. Input Example Result WRS-2 path/row "217/076", "217_076", "217076" Tile footprint, looked up from a Landsat Collection 2 scene Sentinel-2 MGRS tile "23KPQ", "T23KPQ" 109.8 km tile computed offline (within ~50 m of real footprints). Tiles crossing 180° raise ValueError Bounding box [-43.6, -23.1, -43.1, -22.6] That box (lon/lat) Vector file .shp, .gpkg, .geojson, .kml Extent of all features, reprojected to lon/lat Raster file reference.tif Raster extent, reprojected to lon/lat GeoDataFrame / GeoSeries geopandas.read_file(...) Extent, reprojected (no CRS: lon/lat assumed, with a warning) shapely geometry box(...) Its bounds (assumed lon/lat) ee.Geometry Passed through

Sentinel-1 has no fixed tiling grid, so describe Sentinel-1 areas with any of the other inputs. Two offline helpers live in the same module: zeit.gee.roi.roi_bounds(roi) returns the lon/lat bounding box of a local input or a Sentinel-2 tile, and zeit.gee.roi.s2_tile_utm_bounds("23KPQ") returns a tile's exact UTM box, e.g. ("EPSG:32723", (600000, 7390200, 709800, 7500000)).

docs.title: regularize_time_series
docs.text:
zeit.regularize.regularize_time_series(
    cube, freq="16D", method="median", fill=None, max_gap=None, lmbda=10.0,
)

Composites an irregular cube to a fixed time step (16-day, monthly, yearly) with the median, the medoid or the clearest observation of each window, and can fill the periods without a value. Missing values (NaN and the cube's NoData) are left out; periods without observations, and pixels without one in a period, are NaN (an integer cube with NoData keeps its type, with NoData there). Georeferencing and NoData are kept. Stays lazy. Also exported as zeit.regularize_time_series.

Parameter Type Default Description cube DataArray or path required Cube with a time dimension, (time, y, x) or (time, band, y, x), or anything load_raster reads. freq str "16D" pandas frequency: "16D", "1MS", "1YS", … method str "median" "median" (per band), "clearest" or "medoid". "clearest" ranks the dates of a period by the share of the cube's pixels that have every band (the clearest first, the earlier date on a tie) and gives each pixel the observation, with every band, of the first date that has one: a composite is a mosaic of whole observations, of the clearest date where it has data. "medoid" is (the real observation closest to the multi-band median, so a composite's bands come from one date; with one band, the observation closest to the median). Only observations with every band are candidates, and on a tie the earliest wins. The medoid runs in Rust, every pixel in parallel: on 60 dates of 4 bands and 300 × 300 pixels, 0.15 s against 1.0 s for xarray. fill str None What to do with the periods without a value: None leaves them NaN; "linear" interpolates linearly in time between the values before and after (a series' ends stay NaN); "whittaker" fills the same gaps with a Whittaker curve through the values (lmbda) and keeps the values. max_gap float None With fill, the largest gap filled, in days between the value before and the one after; larger gaps stay NaN. None fills any. lmbda float 10.0 fill="whittaker": the curve's smoothness, as in smooth. 
cube_16d = zeit.regularize_time_series(cube, freq="16D", method="medoid")
clear = zeit.regularize_time_series(cube, "MS", method="clearest", fill="linear", max_gap=60)

docs.title: load_raster
docs.text:
zeit.io.load_raster(
    source, *, dates=None, start_year=None, band=None, chunks=None,
    clip=None, masked="auto", pattern=None, date_format=None,
    recursive=False, like=None, crs=None, res=None, resampling="auto",
    validate=None, scale=False, qa=None, qa_rule=None, bands=None,
    window=None, pixel=None, extent=None, tap=False, nodata=None, dtype=None,
    cutline=None,
)

Reads a time series, or a single map, as one georeferenced cube: an xarray.DataArray with dims (time, y, x) (one index) or (time, band, y, x) (several spectral bands), a datetime64 time coordinate, and its CRS, transform and NoData through .rio. The georeferencing and the dates travel with the data, so the algorithms and save_raster need nothing else. Also exported as zeit.load_raster.

It reads:

Source Example Where the dates come from A raster file with one band per date "LT_Stack_NDVI_Rondonia.tif" dates/start_year; the dates save_raster writes into the file; the band descriptions (yr1985, 1985, 2020-01-15, 20200115, or 2020-01-15_red for a time × band stack); a <name>_dates.csv next to it A raster file with several bands per date, date after date "CCDC_Stack_Rondonia.tif" (875 bands) The band descriptions (2020-01-15_red); the dates save_raster writes into the file; a <name>_dates.csv next to it with one date for every few bands (125 dates: 7 bands each, named as the file names them or 1 to 7) A folder, a glob pattern or a list of single-date rasters "tiles/*.tif" The first date in each file name, or pattern= A Zarr store or a NetCDF file "cube.zarr" Its time coordinate An xarray.DataArray or Dataset the output of build_time_series Its time coordinate (lat/lon are renamed y/x) A numpy array (time, y, x) or (time, band, y, x) dates/start_year; like= georeferences it

Without dates, the band axis keeps the name band and the algorithms ask for years/dates. A single band is returned as (y, x).

Parameter Type Default Description source path, list, DataArray, Dataset or ndarray required What to read (see the table above). dates list None Date of each time step: strings, datetimes, years (1985) or fractional years (2020.5). Overrides the dates found in the data. start_year int None Annual series: year of the first time step. band int, str or list None Bands to read: 1-based band numbers in a raster file, band or variable names in a cube or Dataset. chunks "auto", dict None None loads the data into memory; anything else returns a lazy dask-backed cube, read block by block. clip bounds or geometries None Read only a region: (xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax) in the raster's CRS, or polygons (GeoDataFrame, GeoSeries, shapely). masked "auto", bool "auto" "auto": NoData becomes NaN in float rasters, while integer rasters (e.g. NDVI × 10000 in Int16) keep their values and type. True: NaN everywhere (integers become floats). False: values as stored. pattern str None Several files: regular expression with a named group date and optionally band, matched against each file name. date_format str None strptime format of the dates in file names or band descriptions (e.g. "%Y%m%d"). recursive bool False Folders: also search sub-folders. like path, DataArray or Dataset None A reference raster whose grid the result takes (CRS, cells, extent and x/y coordinates), so that the two line up cell by cell; see On the grid of another raster. numpy input: a raster on the same grid whose coordinates and CRS georeference the array. crs str, int, CRS None Without a reference raster: the CRS to reproject to, as gdalwarp -t_srs; see In another CRS or at another resolution. res number or (x, y) None Without a reference raster: the cell size, in the units of crs (or of the data's CRS), as gdalwarp -tr. resampling str "auto" With like, crs or res: "auto" takes the nearest cell for integer rasters and interpolates floats bilinearly (QA bands always take the nearest cell); or a GDAL method: "nearest", "bilinear", "cubic", "cubic_spline", "lanczos", "average", "mode", "min", "max", "med", "q1", "q3", "rms". validate str None "landtrendr", "ccdc" or "cold": warn when the series looks unfit for that algorithm (too few dates, values that do not look scaled). scale bool False Apply the scale_factor and add_offset each band stores (value * scale + offset, after NoData became NaN). Bands without them stay as they are (an Int16 file with no scale keeps its type); the files of a folder each use their own. Not for NetCDF/Zarr stores or DataArray sources, already decoded. Needs masked "auto" or True. Landsat files with a quality band (scales that differ by band) load without rioxarray's "Scales differ across bands" warning, which does not apply when Zeit reads the scales itself (scale=True) or only one band is read. qa band, path, glob, list or DataArray None A quality band: the cube comes back with NaN where the observation is not usable by qa_rule. A band number reads it from the same files, like band= (qa=7: the Fmask of Landsat files of a date); anything else is another source with the same dates and grid, read with the same clip, window/pixel, like... (nearest cell). Integer data becomes float. qa_rule str None With qa: "fmask", "landsat_c2", "nonzero", "scl" or "hls_fmask", see qa_mask. bands dict None Bands by role, {"blue": 1, "red": 3, "nir": 4}: name to band (as band=). Gives a (time, band, y, x) cube whose band coordinate holds the names, in the order of the dict. Not with band. window (col0, row0, col1, row1) None Read only a window of the raster's own pixels (the end is exclusive), no CRS needed. The cells keep their coordinates and transform. A file is read in the window only. Not with clip, like, crs or res. pixel (col, row) None Read one pixel, as a (time,) series ((time, band) with several bands) with scalar x and y coordinates. Only that pixel is read from each file, so it takes a fraction of a second in a stack of many gigabytes. Same restrictions as window. extent (xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax) None Without a reference raster: the extent of the grid, in the CRS of the result, as gdalwarp -te. With res the cells of that size are laid from its top-left corner; without it, the cells of the data (same CRS only), fitted to the extent as gdalwarp does (a whole number of them, a little larger or smaller). With another crs, res is needed. An extent a whole number of cells from the data's only crops it. Not with cutline. tap bool False gdalwarp -tap: the extent aligned to whole cells counted from the origin of the coordinates. Needs res. nodata None, "source" or number None What the cells no data covers hold, and the NoData of the result. None: the data's NoData, else NaN (floats) or the type's extreme (integers). "source": as gdalwarp without -dstnodata: the data's NoData, and when it has none those cells are 0 and the result has no NoData. A number: gdalwarp -dstnodata (the data's NoData cells become it; a value equal to it moves one step). dtype numpy type None The type of the result, as gdalwarp -ot: the warp is done in the wider of the data's type and this one, then rounded (half away from zero) and clamped to it. cutline path, (path, layer), GeoDataFrame, geometries None As gdalwarp -cutline -crop_to_cutline: the cells of the data outside the polygons take no part in the warp (the result there is nodata), and without like the grid is cropped to their extent (and, without res, to the cells of the data entirely inside it). Geometries without a CRS are in the result's. Not with extent.

Returns xarray.DataArray.

ndvi = zeit.load_raster("LT_Stack_NDVI_Rondonia.tif")      # bands yr1985 ... yr2024
ndvi.dims                                                 # ('time', 'y', 'x')
ndvi.time.dt.year.values[[0, -1]]                         # array([1985, 2024])

ndvi = zeit.load_raster("ndvi_stack.tif", start_year=1985, chunks="auto")   # lazy
s2 = zeit.load_raster("S2/", pattern=r"_(?P<date>\d{8})_(?P<band>B\d{2})\.tif$")   # (time, band, y, x)

docs.title: Bands by role, scale, quality band and pixel windows
docs.text:
The options below replace the lines of xarray that a script would otherwise write after reading.

# Landsat files with the bands of a date in each (blue ... swir2, Fmask), reflectance x 10000 with a GDAL scale
cube = zeit.load_raster("landsat/", bands={"blue": 1, "red": 3, "nir": 4}, scale=True,
                        qa=7, qa_rule="fmask")          # (time, band, y, x), NaN where Fmask refuses
ndvi = zeit.normalized_difference(cube, "nir", "red")    # (time, y, x)

stack = "LT_Stack_NDVI_Rondonia.tif"                     # 40 bands, 20 GB-class stacks work the same
series = zeit.load_raster(stack, pixel=(120, 80))        # (time,), reads that pixel only
block = zeit.load_raster(stack, window=(100, 60, 140, 100))   # (time, 40, 40)

window and pixel count the columns and rows of the file's own grid (column first), so they also work on series with no CRS, where clip= cannot. Quality bands take the pixel or window too, and bands= reads each band with the same options.

docs.title: On the grid of another raster
docs.text:
like= puts the data on the grid of a reference raster, reprojecting and resampling it: Landsat at 30 m onto a Sentinel-2 grid at 10 m, a land-cover map onto the grid of a cube, or a folder of scenes from different orbits or UTM zones onto one grid.

s2 = zeit.load_raster("S2_ndvi.tif")
landsat = zeit.load_raster("landsat_ndvi.tif", like=s2)              # bilinear for floats
classes = zeit.load_raster("mapbiomas_2020.tif", like=s2)           # nearest cell for integers
scenes = zeit.load_raster("scenes/", like="S2_ndvi.tif", chunks="auto")   # each file onto the grid
bool((landsat.x == s2.x).all())                                     # True: they line up
  • Every date on its own. Each date (and band) is resampled with its own NoData, as GDAL warping that date alone: a cloud in one date never leaks into the interpolation of another. (GDAL's warp of a multiband raster takes a cell as valid when any band is, so a cloudy cell of one date enters the bilinear or average of that date and spreads its NoData.)
  • GDAL's resampling, faster. The kernels are GDAL's (gdalwarpkernel.cpp, ported to Rust from landschaft's C++ port), run in parallel; the source coordinates of the cells are computed once for every date. On a cube of 240 dates of 1000 × 1000 cells (UTM to EPSG:3035), nearest takes 0.5 s, bilinear 0.7 s and average 0.9 s, against 2.4 s, 22.6 s and 6.4 s for rioxarray's reproject_match.
  • The same values however it runs: in memory, lazily (chunks=) or from a file, with any number of threads. A file is read only in the window the grid sees, and a lazy cube stays lazy.
  • No warp when it is not needed: a grid with the same CRS and cells, a whole number of cells apart, is only a crop (and padding with NoData) of the data.
  • Cells outside the data are NoData (NaN for floats; integer rasters keep their NoData value, or get the largest value of unsigned types and the smallest of signed ones).

docs.title: The options of gdalwarp
docs.text:
extent=, tap=, nodata=, dtype= and cutline= add gdalwarp's -te, -tap, -dstnodata, -ot and -cutline to crs=, res= and like=, with the same grid, type, NoData and values (nearest cell: the same cells; bilinear and cubic: the same within 1e-5 of the values; see below). The defaults are unchanged: nodata=None still gives NaN or the type's extreme outside the data, where gdalwarp writes 0; pass nodata="source" for gdalwarp's.

# Janus' "Reproject, resample, clip" with aligned pixels, a NoData value and a cutline
zeit.save_raster(zeit.load_raster("ndvi.tif", crs="EPSG:4326", res=0.0003, tap=True, nodata=-9999,
                                  cutline="zones.gpkg", resampling="bilinear"), "ndvi_zone.tif")

Notes on how close it is to gdalwarp:

  • A reprojection places the cells with the coordinates of gdalwarp's approximate transformer (-et 0.125, GDAL's GDALApproxTransform: exact at the ends and middle of a row of the result, a line between them where it is within the tolerance), so every method (the area ones from the corners of their cells, as GDAL approximates them) gives the same cells and values as gdalwarp's default, bit for bit, for a result that gdalwarp warps in one piece (it splits one that needs more than 64 MB of working memory, or whose source window is mostly outside the source, and approximates each piece in its own rows; then a few cells, 0.01 % to 1 %, take a neighbouring cell).
  • cutline is applied as gdalwarp does, to the cells of the source: those outside the polygons do not take part in the interpolation (cells whose nearest source cells are outside are NoData).
  • crs with extent or cutline needs res; and cutline with extent is an error, because gdalwarp's -crop_to_cutline replaces -te. tap without a extent/cutline widens the extent of the data to whole cells from the origin of the coordinates, as gdalwarp does. Without extent, gdalwarp drops a border row or column of the result that falls entirely outside the source (GDAL 3.8 and later); so does Zeit.

docs.title: In another CRS or at another resolution
docs.text:
Without a reference raster, crs= and res= make the grid gdalwarp -t_srs crs -tr res would: the extent that covers the data in that CRS, and either cells of res laid from its top-left corner or GDAL's suggested resolution. A folder's grid covers all of its files, at the finest of their resolutions, as gdalwarp does with several inputs. The warp is the same as with like=, so everything above applies.

albers = zeit.load_raster("ndvi_stack.tif", crs="EPSG:5880", res=30)    # reprojected, 30 m cells
coarse = zeit.load_raster("ndvi_stack.tif", res=250, resampling="average")   # same CRS, 250 m
scenes = zeit.load_raster("scenes/", crs=32722, chunks="auto")          # two UTM zones onto one

The cells start at the corner of the data's extent, so two rasters loaded this way do not necessarily line up: to combine sources, load the first with crs=/res= and the others with like= it.

docs.title: save_raster
docs.text:
zeit.io.save_raster(
    data, path, *, like=None, crs=None, transform=None, nodata=None,
    dtype=None, band_names=None, compress="deflate", driver=None,
    reference_cube=None, categories=None, colors=None,
)

Writes a map, a stack or a result so that GIS software and load_raster read it back as it was: georeferencing, NoData, band names and dates. Returns the path written. Also exported as zeit.save_raster.

  • A DataArray brings its own georeferencing (.rio, or its x/y coordinates); a numpy or dask array takes it from like= (a raster or a path), or from crs and transform.
  • A time axis becomes the band descriptions (1985, … for annual series, 2020-01-15, … otherwise) and the ZEIT_TIME metadata tag, so load_raster gets the time coordinate back. A (time, band, y, x) cube is written as 2020-01-15_red, 2020-01-15_nir, …
  • More leading dims become one band per combination, named by joining their labels: CCDC's coefs (segment, band, coef, y, x) is written as 1_blue_a0, 1_blue_c1, … Dates (datetime64, such as CCDC's t_break) are written as decimal years, NaN where there is none.
  • A Dataset or a dict of maps (e.g. the result of extract_events, bfast_monitor or mann_kendall) becomes a folder with one GeoTIFF per variable when path has no extension, or one multi-band file named by variable when it ends in .tif. Variables with a leading dim get one band per label: each phenology metric (year, y, x) is written with bands 2010, 2011, …
  • Floats with NaN get NaN as NoData (or nodata, which then replaces the NaN); bool is written as uint8 and 64-bit integers as the smallest integer type that holds them.
  • GeoTIFFs are compressed with the predictor that suits the type, tiled when larger than 256 × 256 and BigTIFF when needed; dask arrays are written block by block. The format follows the extension (.tif, .img, .nc, .zarr, …) or driver ("COG" for a Cloud-Optimised GeoTIFF). Missing folders are created.
Parameter Type Default Description data DataArray, Dataset, dict, numpy or dask array required What to write: (y, x), (band\|time, y, x), (time, band, y, x) or more leading dims. path str or Path required Output file, or folder for a Dataset/dict. Without an extension, .tif is added. like path or DataArray None A raster on the same grid whose CRS and transform georeference data. crs str, int, CRS None Coordinate reference system; overrides that of data and like. transform Affine None Affine transform; overrides that of data and like. nodata float None NoData value; overrides that of data. NaN in floats are written as this value. dtype str None Data type to write (default: the data's). Floats cast to integers get nodata (or the type's maximum) where they are NaN. band_names list of str None Band descriptions; by default the dates of a time axis or the labels of a band axis. compress str "deflate" GeoTIFF compression: "deflate", "lzw", "zstd", None… driver str None GDAL driver when the extension is not enough; "COG" writes a Cloud-Optimised GeoTIFF. reference_cube path or DataArray None Deprecated name of like. categories dict None The classes of a classified map, {value: name}, written as the first band's category names (GDAL's SetCategoryNames; for a GeoTIFF, in the .aux.xml beside it), where QGIS and Janus read them. Values are non-negative integers; a value without a name gets an empty one. One map only, not a dict or Dataset. colors dict None The classes' colours, {value: colour}, with the colour as "#RRGGBB", "#RRGGBBAA" or an (r, g, b[, a]) tuple of 0-255, written as the first band's colour table. Needs a uint8 or uint16 map and a GeoTIFF or COG. A GeoTIFF palette keeps no per-class alpha.

Returns pathlib.Path.

ndvi = zeit.load_raster("LT_Stack_NDVI_Rondonia.tif")
zeit.save_raster(ndvi.sel(time="2020"), "ndvi_2020.tif")       # georeferencing from the cube
zeit.save_raster(loss, "lt_rondonia")                          # Dataset of maps: one GeoTIFF each
zeit.save_raster(yod_array, "year_of_loss.tif", like=ndvi, nodata=0)     # numpy map
zeit.save_raster(lc, "lc.tif", nodata=0, categories={1: "forest", 2: "water"}, colors={1: "#2ca02c", 2: "#1f77b4"})

docs.title: build_vrt
docs.text:
zeit._vrt.build_vrt(
    sources, path, *, separate=False, extent=None, res=None,
    resampling="nearest", band_names=None, wavelengths=None,
)

Writes a VRT, a small XML file that GDAL, rasterio, QGIS and load_raster read as a raster, of tiles mosaicked and bands stacked, with no pixel copied. It is what gdal.BuildVRT writes (the same grid, the same sources' windows, the same values), without GDAL's Python bindings. Returns the path written. Also exported as zeit.build_vrt.

  • sources is a list of files (the tiles of a scene, mosaicked; the bands of the files are kept), a list of files with separate=True (each file is one band, stacked), or a list of lists of files (one output band per inner list, made of the tiles of that band).
  • Where tiles overlap the later file wins, except where it holds NoData. Pixels no tile covers are NoData, or 0 for a band without one. A band has a NoData value when every file of it has one. The files must share a CRS and be north-up.
  • The source files are referred to by absolute path.
Parameter Type Default Description sources list of paths required Files, or lists of files, as above. path str or Path required The .vrt to write. Missing folders are created. separate bool False A flat list of files: each is one band (its first), stacked. extent (xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax) None The VRT's extent; None: the union of the files. res float or (xres, yres) None The VRT's pixel; None: the finest pixel of the files. resampling str "nearest" How a source of another pixel size or alignment is read: "nearest", "bilinear", "cubic", "average", "mode", … band_names list of str None The bands' descriptions; by default the first file's. wavelengths dict None {band name: nm}, written as the wavelength and wavelength_units metadata of the bands with that name.

Returns pathlib.Path.

vrt = zeit.build_vrt([["B04_a.tif", "B04_b.tif"], ["B08_a.tif", "B08_b.tif"]], "scene.vrt",
                     extent=(600000, 7396400, 606000, 7400000), res=30,
                     band_names=["B04", "B08"], wavelengths={"B04": 664.6, "B08": 832.8})
cube = zeit.load_raster(vrt)

docs.title: get_georef
docs.text:
zeit.io.get_georef(reference_cube)

Extracts {"crs": ..., "transform": ...} from a rasterio dataset or an xarray object. Handy for snic_to_polygons or custom writers. Also exported as zeit.get_georef.

Parameter Type Default Description reference_cube rasterio dataset or xr.DataArray required Object to read the georeferencing from.

docs.title: Quality bands to weights
docs.text:
Decoders written from the products' documentation (the MODIS MOD13 and MOD09 user guides, ESA's description of the Sentinel-2 SCL), with weights of Zeit's own. Each turns a sensor's QA band into per-observation reliability weights in [0, 1] for the weights= of zeit.smooth and zeit.phenology. A QA cube (a DataArray, or a raster path) gives a weights cube with its dims, dates and georeferencing, lazy if it was, ready to pass along with the data it describes; the raster's NoData (and NaN) get the weight 0. A numpy array gives a numpy array. All three are exported at the top level.

cube = zeit.build_time_series(..., bands=["red", "nir", "scl"])
ndvi = zeit.compute_indices(cube, ["NDVI"]).sel(band="NDVI")
weights = zeit.qc_sentinel2_scl(cube.sel(band="scl"))     # (time, y, x), on the cube's grid
pheno = zeit.phenology(ndvi, weights=weights)

docs.title: qa_mask
docs.text:
zeit.qc.qa_mask(qa, rule)

The observations a quality band keeps, as a boolean "usable" mask (the rules Janus applies to a quality band). A code counts when it is a number of 0 or more (fractions are cut); NaN, negative values and the raster's NoData are never usable. Exported as zeit.qa_mask; load_raster(..., qa=, qa_rule=) applies it while reading.

Parameter Type Default Description qa array, DataArray or path required The quality band (lazy if the DataArray is). rule str required "fmask": 0 clear land and 1 water usable (2 shadow, 3 snow, 4 cloud, 255 fill masked). "landsat_c2": QA_PIXEL bits 0 fill, 1 dilated cloud, 3 cloud, 4 shadow and 5 snow clear (code & 0x3B == 0). "nonzero": any code but 0. "scl": Sentinel-2 SCL 4 vegetation, 5 bare soil, 6 water. "hls_fmask": HLS v2.0 Fmask bits 1 to 4 (cloud, adjacent, shadow, snow or ice) clear, and not 255.

Returns a boolean array or DataArray with the input's dims and coordinates.

usable = zeit.qa_mask(cube.sel(band="fmask"), "fmask")
clear = cube.sel(band="nir").where(usable)

docs.title: qa_to_fmask
docs.text:
zeit.qc.qa_to_fmask(qa, rule)

The Fmask codes of a quality band: 0 clear, 1 water, 2 shadow, 3 snow, 4 cloud, 255 no data, the codes the qa= of ccdc and sccd read. Same rule names as qa_mask (and fmask <= 1 is exactly its mask). A code counts when it is a number of 0 or more (fractions are cut); NaN, negative values and the raster's NoData are 255. Exported as zeit.qa_to_fmask.

Parameter Type Default Description qa array, DataArray or path required The quality band (lazy if the DataArray is). rule str required "fmask": the codes as they are (anything but 0-4 and 255 becomes 255). "landsat_c2": QA_PIXEL bit 0 (fill) 255; bits 1 and 3 (dilated cloud, cloud) 4; bit 4 (shadow) 2; bit 5 (snow) 3; bit 7 (water) 1; else 0 (the first that applies, in this order). "scl": Sentinel-2 SCL 4 and 5 are 0, 6 (water) 1, 2 and 3 (shadows) 2, 11 (snow or ice) 3, 7 to 10 (unclassified, clouds, cirrus) 4, the rest 255. "hls_fmask": 255 is 255; bits 1 and 2 (cloud, adjacent) 4; bit 3 (shadow) 2; bit 4 (snow or ice) 3; bit 5 (water) 1; else 0. "nonzero": 0 is 4, any other code 0.

Returns a uint8 array or DataArray (named fmask) with the input's dims and coordinates.

qa = zeit.load_raster("landsat/", band=7, masked=True, pixel=(896, 186))   # QA_PIXEL
segments = zeit.ccdc(bands_cube, qa=zeit.qa_to_fmask(qa, "landsat_c2"), scale="auto")

docs.title: qc_sentinel2_scl
docs.text:
zeit.qc.qc_sentinel2_scl(scl, wmin=0.2, wmid=0.5, wmax=1.0)

Sentinel-2 L2A Scene Classification Layer: vegetation and bare soil get wmax; water and unclassified get wmid; shadows, medium- and high-probability cloud, thin cirrus and snow get wmin; no data, saturated or defective pixels and codes outside 0-11 get 0.

Parameter Type Default Description scl array, DataArray or path required SCL values, any shape. wmin, wmid, wmax float 0.2, 0.5, 1.0 Weights for bad, doubtful and good observations.

docs.title: qc_modis_summary
docs.text:
zeit.qc.qc_modis_summary(qa, wmin=0.2, wmid=0.5, wmax=1.0)

MOD13 "SummaryQA" / pixel reliability: 0 good → wmax, 1 marginal → wmid, 2 snow and 3 cloudy → wmin, fill → 0.

Parameter Type Default Description qa array, DataArray or path required SummaryQA values, any shape. wmin, wmid, wmax float 0.2, 0.5, 1.0 Weights for bad, doubtful and good observations. 
from zeit.qc import qc_modis_summary

weights = qc_modis_summary(qa_cube)          # a DataArray like qa_cube

docs.title: qc_modis_state
docs.text:
zeit.qc.qc_modis_state(qa, wmin=0.2, wmid=0.5, wmax=1.0)

MOD09 500 m 16-bit "State QA": decodes cloud state, cloud shadow, aerosol quantity and snow/ice bits.

Parameter Type Default Description qa array, DataArray or path required State QA values, any shape. wmin, wmid, wmax float 0.2, 0.5, 1.0 Weights for bad, doubtful and good observations.

docs.title: Embeddings
docs.text:
The yearly embeddings of Earth observation foundation models, TESSERA and Google's AlphaEarth, as zeit cubes: one vector per 10 m pixel and year that classification, sampling, segmentation and clustering take as they are; plus similarity search and change from year to year.

Both products summarise a whole year of imagery in a vector per pixel, made by a model trained on a great many pixels; what they are made for, in both papers, is mapping from few labelled samples with simple classifiers. zeit reads them as a (time, band, y, x) cube, band the dimensions (A00, A01...), and records in its attributes which embeddings it holds; save_raster keeps that, train_classifier and zeit.ai.train record it in the model, and classify and zeit.ai.predict refuse a cube of other embeddings (another product, version or variant is another space). Tutorial: Embeddings (TESSERA, AlphaEarth).

TESSERA AlphaEarth Foundations Dimensions 128 64 (each embedding has length 1) Cells, years 10 m, 2017–2025 (v1.1) 10 m, 2017–2025 Made from Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 Sentinel-1, Sentinel-2, Landsat and more Read from the TESSERA Zarr store, through geotessera (installed with zeit on Python 3.12+) open COGs on Source Cooperative (free, no account: the default), or Earth Engine Licence CC0 1.0 CC-BY 4.0: "The AlphaEarth Foundations Satellite Embedding dataset is produced by Google and Google DeepMind." Cite Feng et al. (2025), arXiv:2506.20380 Brown et al. (2025), arXiv:2507.22291

What not to run on embeddings

An embedding has no physical unit and no seasonal signal: the algorithms that fit one (LandTrendr, CCDC, BFAST, Mann-Kendall, phenology, TWDTW, smoothing, Tmask, indices, unmixing, CODED, regularize_time_series) refuse a cube of embeddings with a message saying what to use instead.

docs.title: load_embeddings
docs.text:
zeit.load_embeddings(
    region=None, *, source, years=None, like=None, crs=None, res=None,
    resampling="auto", version=None, variant=None, depth=None,
    backend=None, store=None, chunks="auto", cache_dir=None,
)

Reads the embeddings of a product over a region as a georeferenced cube, lazily by default (one year and every dimension of 512 x 512 cells for TESSERA, 1024 x 1024 for AlphaEarth, on the products' own blocks). A region within one UTM zone keeps the zone's CRS and the cells the embeddings were made on, so the two products line up cell by cell; south of the equator that is the southern UTM CRS (TESSERA stores it in the northern one, with negative northings: the same cells). Also exported as zeit.load_embeddings; CLI: zeit embeddings.

Parameter Type Default Description region bounds, GeoDataFrame, path or geometries None (west, south, east, north) in longitude and latitude, a GeoDataFrame/GeoSeries or vector file in any CRS, or shapely geometries in longitude and latitude. Cells outside polygons are NaN; points (e.g. training samples) read the box around them. Optional with like. source str required "tessera" or "alphaearth". years int, list or range None The years (default: all the product has). like path, DataArray or Dataset None A raster whose grid the result takes (its extent, if region is not given), as in load_raster. crs, res None Without like: CRS and cell size of the result (default 10 m). Needed for a region across UTM zones. resampling str "auto" With like, crs or res: "auto" takes the nearest cell (interpolated embeddings are vectors the model never made), and the mean of the cells ("average") when the target cells are at least 1.5 times larger. Or any method of load_raster. version, variant str None TESSERA: dataset version (default "v1.1", the complete global run) and variant (default: the version's). depth int None TESSERA v2: only the first depth dimensions (a Matryoshka prefix, published as an array of its own). backend str None AlphaEarth: "source.coop" (default: the open COGs, free, no account or quota) or "gee" (the GOOGLE/SATELLITE_EMBEDDING/V1/ANNUAL collection, with an Earth Engine session up, downloaded into cache_dir; it uses the account's quota). store URL, path or zarr store None A copy of the product to read: TESSERA, a Zarr store (read without geotessera when local); AlphaEarth, a folder or URL with aef_index.parquet and the COGs in <year>/<zone>/. chunks "auto", None or dict "auto" None reads it all into memory. cache_dir path None Where downloads are kept: the AlphaEarth index (78 MB, refreshed monthly) and Earth Engine downloads. Default ~/.cache/zeit/embeddings.

Returns an xarray.DataArray (time, band, y, x) float32 named embeddings, NaN where there is no embedding, with attributes embedding_source, embedding_version, embedding_variant (what a model checks), embedding_model, embedding_dimensions, embedding_license and the citation (and attribution, for AlphaEarth).

import zeit

emb = zeit.load_embeddings("aoi.gpkg", source="tessera", years=range(2018, 2025))
aef = zeit.load_embeddings((-63.0, -10.0, -62.9, -9.9), source="alphaearth", years=2024)
on_landsat = zeit.load_embeddings(source="alphaearth", like=landsat_cube, years=2020)   # 30 m, averaged

The blocks last read are kept as they were downloaded (int8, up to 1 GB; the environment variable ZEIT_EMBEDDING_CACHE_MB changes the limit, 0 turns it off), so a lazy cube computed twice is downloaded once: the principal components zeit.plot fits and then its frames, or the blocks under training points and then the classification of the same region. Reading is bound by the servers' throughput (about 4 MB/s of int8 from Europe), not by the computation.

docs.title: similarity
docs.text:
zeit.similarity(emb, ref, *, by=None, year=None, metric="cosine")

How much each pixel looks like a reference: "find more places like these". The reference is the mean embedding of some samples (every cell of a polygon) in one year, compared with every year of the cube, which shows where it appears over time. Also exported as zeit.similarity.

Parameter Type Default Description emb DataArray required Embeddings (time, band, y, x) or (band, y, x). ref GeoDataFrame, path or sequence required Points or polygons (any CRS), or one embedding (as many values as band). by str None A column of ref: one reference, and one map, per value (e.g. each class). year int None The year the samples' embeddings are taken from (default: the last). metric str "cosine" "cosine": cosine similarity (1 for the same direction); "euclidean": the distance.

Returns an xarray.DataArray (time, y, x) float32 (with a class dim first with by), lazy when the cube is.

mines = zeit.similarity(emb, "known_mines.gpkg", year=2024)
zeit.plot(mines)                                            # where it looks like a mine, year by year

docs.title: embedding_change
docs.text:
zeit.embedding_change(emb, *, metric="cosine", baseline="previous")

How far each pixel's embedding moved from one year to another. extract_events turns it into one event per pixel in the schema of the other change algorithms, so agreement compares it with LandTrendr, CCDC, BFAST or CODED and the validation functions take it as it is. Also exported as zeit.embedding_change.

Parameter Type Default Description emb DataArray required Embeddings (time, band, y, x) with at least two years. metric str "cosine" "cosine": 1 - cos of the angle between the embeddings (0 the same direction, 2 opposite); or "euclidean". baseline str or int "previous" "previous": each year against the year before it; "first": against the first; or a year to compare every other year with.

Returns an xarray.Dataset:

Variable Meaning distance (time, y, x): the distance of each year to its baseline. noise (y, x): the median of the pixel's distances, its usual movement from year to year.

With baseline="previous", extract_events gives magnitude (the distance), dsnr (the distance over the noise), yod (the year before the first embedding that shows the change) and date (January 1 of that one); events have no direction (event_type="any"). An embedding summarises a year, so a change in the middle of one shows partly in it and partly in the next: compare with other algorithms with tolerance=1.

Each product has its own scale of distances: year to year, TESSERA's pixels move a cosine distance of about 0.05–0.1 and AlphaEarth's about 0.02, so a threshold for one is not one for the other. min_magnitude (e.g. 0.3 for TESSERA, 0.2 for AlphaEarth, for clearing of forest) or sort_by="dsnr" with a threshold on dsnr keep the real changes.

change = zeit.embedding_change(emb)
events = zeit.extract_events(change, min_magnitude=0.3)
zeit.agreement(events, zeit.extract_events(zeit.landtrendr(ndvi)), tolerance=1)

docs.title: Many Tiles & Helpers
docs.text:
Run a command on every tile of a folder, on this computer and on other computers of the local network that lend themselves to it. No cluster to set up: one command on each helper, one on the computer that has the tiles. Tutorial: Many tiles on several computers.

# On each computer that helps (once: zeit worker --join <code>; see invite_helpers)
zeit.run_worker()

# On the computer with the tiles
zeit.run_tiles("landtrendr", "nbr_tiles/", "lt_out/", helpers=True, max_segments=6)
zeit.run_tiles("landtrendr", "nbr_tiles/", "lt_out/", helpers=True, local=False)   # only coordinate

The same is available from the terminal: zeit landtrendr nbr_tiles/ lt_out/ --helpers, zeit worker, zeit helpers invite (see the CLI).

docs.title: run_tiles
docs.text:
zeit.run_tiles(
    command, inputs, output_dir, *, helpers=False, local=True,
    local_cores=None, port=47801, compress_transfers=True,
    verbose=True, shard=None, **options,
)

Runs a command of the zeit command line on every tile, writing <output_dir>/<tile name>/ with the command's outputs. Each tile runs in its own process, on this computer or on a helper, with all the cores it was given (the algorithms' threads). The largest tiles go first.

  • Resumable. A finished tile is moved into place in one step, with a record of the options. Running the same call again skips the tiles already done, so an interrupted run continues where it stopped; other options for the same output folder raise an error rather than mixing results.
  • Helpers pull. Each helper asks for a tile when it has room and fetches the next one while it processes the current one, so fast and slow machines balance by themselves. It reads a tile straight from shared storage (a NAS) when it sees the same file there, otherwise this computer sends it (compressed, when the file is not); tiles it already has from an earlier run are not sent again.
  • Results. A helper that sees the output folder too (a NAS) writes its results straight into it; otherwise it sends them back.
  • No waiting for the slowest. Near the end, an idle machine that would finish a straggler clearly sooner runs it too, and the first result wins. The last tile stays on this computer when it would finish it before a helper.
  • Failures. A tile that fails is tried again on another machine; after two failures it is given up and reported, and the other tiles go on. A helper that stops responding gives its tiles back to the queue.
  • Warnings. It says when the tiles are float32 without compression (they cross the network at full size), when the network is the bottleneck (the helpers wait for tiles more than they process them), and how to make helpers appear when none has joined.
Parameter Type Default Description command str required A command that reads one raster: "landtrendr", "ccdc", "bfast_monitor", "bfast_lite", "bfast", "mann_kendall", "phenology", "smooth", "tmask", "twdtw", "snic", "classify", "som", "coded", "bandpass_adjust". inputs path, glob, list or TileSources required A folder (its .tif files), a glob pattern ("tiles/LT_*.tif"), a list of files, a .txt file of URLs (one per line), or tiles each computer fetches or builds for itself: tile_urls, stac_tiles, gee_tiles. Two tiles cannot have the same name. output_dir path required Where the per-tile folders are written. helpers bool False Also send tiles to the computers of this computer's group running zeit worker. local bool True Process tiles here too. False (with helpers=True): only hand out tiles and collect the results, leaving this computer free. local_cores int None Cores for the tiles processed here; None: as n_jobs=-1, all but one, or all of a cluster job's. port int 47801 TCP port the helpers connect to. compress_transfers bool True Send a tile stored without compression as a lossless ZSTD copy: the same values, fewer bytes on the network (1.43× fewer for Landsat NBR in float32, made at ~300 MB/s). verbose bool True Print the progress, the helpers that join or leave, and the warnings. shard str None "i/n": process part i (from 0) of n of the tiles, tile k (in the order of inputs) being part k mod n's. Inside a Slurm job array, None takes the task's part (see Clusters). **options The command's options as keyword arguments, named as in the CLI with underscores: max_segments=6, event_type="gain", monitor_start_time="2020-01-01". A file used by every tile (patterns= of twdtw, dates_file= of ccdc, model= of classify, training= of coded) is sent to the helpers; a file that belongs to one raster (weights=, samples=) cannot be used.

Returns a TileRunResult: done (the tiles processed now), skipped (already done before), failed (tile → error), machines (computer → tiles processed), seconds, and ok (no failures). On SIGTERM (a scheduler's warning before a job's time limit) it raises zeit._tiles.Stopped, a KeyboardInterrupt whose done lists the tiles finished before: the tiles being processed are dropped, the finished ones kept.

result = zeit.run_tiles("bfast_monitor", "ndvi_16day/", "monitor/", helpers=True,
                        monitor_start_time="2022-01-01", h=0.25)
if not result.ok:
    print(result.failed)          # {"tile_07": "...the command's last lines of output..."}

docs.title: Tiles each computer builds
docs.text:
Instead of files on this computer, the tiles can be recipes: every computer then downloads or builds the tiles it processes, into its own cache (kept for the next run), and nothing passes through this computer. A recipe is data, a kind and its options checked against a fixed list, never code. It pays off when the computers have independent internet links: helpers on this computer's local network most likely share its link, and the run says so.

tiles = zeit.stac_tiles(["21LYG", "21LZG", "22LBM"], index="NBR", bands=["nir08", "swir22"],
                        start_year=1985, end_year=2024, source="planetary_computer")
zeit.run_tiles("landtrendr", tiles, "lt_out/", helpers=True)

By default an index is written as int16, the index × 10000 with NoData −32768: what LandTrendr reads directly, and a third of the bytes of float32 once compressed.

docs.title: tile_urls
docs.text:
zeit.tile_urls(urls)

Rasters each computer downloads for itself: https:// (a plain download) or a bucket GDAL reads (s3://, gs://, az://, with the usual credentials in the environment). Only URLs: a recipe never names a file of the computer that builds it.

Parameter Type Default Description urls list or dict required URLs, each tile named after its file, or {name: url}.

docs.title: stac_tiles
docs.text:
zeit.stac_tiles(
    tiles, *, index=None, scale=10000.0, dtype="int16", **options,
)

Annual composites from a STAC catalog, built by each computer for the tiles it processes with build_annual_composites, optionally reduced to one index with compute_indices.

Parameter Type Default Description tiles list or dict required Sentinel-2 tile ids ("23KPQ"), (min_lon, min_lat, max_lon, max_lat) boxes, vector or raster files (their extent), or {name: one of these}. Each becomes a box in lon/lat. index str None "NBR", "NDVI", ...: one index instead of the bands. scale float 10000.0 With an integer dtype, values are written as value * scale. dtype str "int16" "int16", "int32" (NoData: the type's minimum) or "float32" (values as they are). **options Of build_annual_composites: source, collection, start_year, end_year, season, bands (required), cloud_cover_max, method, apply_cloud_mask, resolution, epsg, chunksize. Without epsg, each tile is built in its own UTM zone, so resolution (30 by default) is in metres.

docs.title: gee_tiles
docs.text:
zeit.gee_tiles(
    tiles, *, start_year, end_year, index="NBR", project=None,
    method="auto", scale=10000.0, dtype="int16",
)

Annual medoid composites from Earth Engine, downloaded by each computer for the tiles it processes (download_gee_timeseries with composite_type="annual") and stacked into one file per tile. Every computer needs Earth Engine credentials (earthengine authenticate). Earth Engine limits concurrent requests per project, so computers using the same project share that limit.

Parameter Type Default Description tiles list or dict required Landsat WRS-2 ids ("217/076", named 217_076), Sentinel-2 ids, boxes, or {name: tile}. start_year, end_year int required The years, inclusive. index str "NBR" One index, or None for the six surface reflectance bands. project str None Google Cloud project for Earth Engine. method str "auto" Download method of download_gee_image: "auto", "direct" or "drive". scale, dtype 10000.0, "int16" As in stac_tiles.

docs.title: run_worker
docs.text:
zeit.run_worker(
    *, cores=None, connect=None, join=None, maps=(), cache_dir=None,
    cache_gb=20.0,
)

Lends this computer to its group until Ctrl+C: it waits for a computer of the group that runs tiles, processes the tiles it gets, and waits again. The same as zeit worker in a terminal. A helper only opens outgoing connections and only runs zeit's own commands with the options it receives (never code sent by another computer), keeps the computer from sleeping while it works, and sets what the OpenMP runtime needs on macOS.

Both computers need the same zeit: a helper with another version (or other code, as in a development install) is told which version to install and gets no tiles.

Parameter Type Default Description cores int None Cores to lend; None: as n_jobs=-1. connect str None The coordinator's address, "192.168.1.10" or "host:port", when the broadcasts of the local network do not reach it (another subnet, a VPN). join str None The invitation code shown by invite_helpers / zeit helpers invite on a computer of the group, the first time only. maps list of str () Where shared folders are mounted here, as "SRC=DST": a tile the coordinator sees under SRC is read under DST, e.g. "Z:\\=/mnt/nas" or "\\\\nas\\tiles=/Volumes/tiles". Mapped Windows drives are sent as their UNC paths, which Windows helpers read without a map. cache_dir path None Where received tiles are kept; None: the user's cache folder. cache_gb float 20.0 Space the kept tiles may take; the least recently used go first.

docs.title: invite_helpers
docs.text:
zeit.invite_helpers(minutes=10.0, *, port=47801)

Shows an invitation code (such as K7QM-2XDP) and, for minutes, lets other computers join this computer's group with zeit worker --join <code>. The same as zeit helpers invite. Returns the names of the computers that joined. A computer joins once; afterwards zeit worker is enough. Any computer of the group can then run tiles with the others' help, and invite more.

Parameter Type Default Description minutes float 10.0 How long the code is valid. port int 47801 TCP port of the invitation.

Security

The code is only an invitation: it authenticates one pairing (over TLS, with a key stretched by scrypt; ten wrong codes close the invitation), in which the newcomer receives the group's random 256-bit secret. Every later connection proves the secret both ways, bound to the coordinator's TLS certificate, so another machine of the network can neither pose as a member nor read the tiles. The secret is kept in the user's configuration folder (%APPDATA%\zeit on Windows, ~/.config/zeit elsewhere); zeit helpers leave forgets it.

docs.title: Clusters
docs.text:
On a cluster the tiles go to the tasks of a job array rather than to helpers (whose broadcasts a cluster's network does not carry; helpers=True inside a job is refused). Every task runs the same command, and takes its part of the tiles by itself:

#SBATCH --array=0-49 --cpus-per-task=16
zeit landtrendr tiles/ out/ --tiles      # task i processes tiles i, i + 50, i + 100, ...
  • The split. Tile k, in the order of the inputs, goes to part k mod n, n being the number of tasks. Static, so it needs no lock on the shared file system (NFS and Lustre differ on them). The first task keeps the split in out/.zeit-tiles/split.json, so that tasks submitted again later (--array=3,17,41) take the same tiles. Other schedulers: shard="i/n" (--shard), e.g. --shard $PBS_ARRAY_INDEX/50.
  • Shared output folder. Each run keeps its unfinished work apart (out/.zeit-partial/<job>_<task>), and a finished tile moves into place atomically.
  • The record. out/.zeit-tiles/ keeps the tiles of the run, what each task finished, what failed (with the error, and the tile's log in logs/) and whether it was stopped: zeit tiles status reads it.
  • Time limits. On SIGTERM (#SBATCH --signal=B:TERM@120, two minutes before the limit) the tile at work is dropped, its folder deleted, and with --requeue the task requeues itself (scontrol requeue) to continue with the tiles left.

zeit slurm writes the job script; the tutorial is Zeit on a cluster (HPC, Slurm).

docs.title: Threads (n_jobs)
docs.text:
Every function with n_jobs counts the threads of n_jobs=-1 (the default) with one rule, the same in Python and in the compiled core. A positive n_jobs is the count. Otherwise, the first that applies:

  1. ZEIT_NUM_THREADS, as it is. Tile runs set it for each tile's process.
  2. In a worker of dask.distributed, the worker's threads (--nthreads, threads_per_worker), and not the OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 its nanny sets for the BLAS libraries.
  3. zeit config threads N, the user's own setting, outside a batch job.
  4. OMP_NUM_THREADS, as it is.
  5. The job's processors from its scheduler's variables, when the processors this process may run on are more (a cluster that does not confine its jobs): SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK, or without --cpus-per-task SLURM_CPUS_ON_NODE and SLURM_JOB_CPUS_PER_NODE; NCPUS (PBS Pro) and PBS_NUM_PPN (Torque); LSB_DJOB_NUMPROC (LSF).
  6. The processors this process may run on: its affinity (taskset, srun --cpu-bind) and the cgroup quota a scheduler or a container sets. In a job of Slurm, PBS or LSF (SLURM_JOB_ID, PBS_JOBID, LSB_JOBID), or when the process is confined to fewer than the machine has, all of them are used: they were given to it. Otherwise they are shared with whoever else is logged in to the machine (below), and on a computer of one's own one is kept free, so it stays responsive.

A machine several people use at once. On a Windows server reached by Remote Desktop, a Linux server reached by SSH, or a cluster's login node, -1 divides the processors by the distinct users with an active session: 48 processors and 3 people logged in give 16 threads each, and the same machine at night, with one person, gives 47. Zeit counts users, not sessions (the same user in two windows counts once), and only active ones: on Windows the sessions quser lists as Active (a Remote Desktop closed without signing out is Disconnected and does not count), on Linux the logins of utmp (what who lists) or, without it, systemd-logind's sessions. Neither needs an administrator. The count is read again every 30 seconds. On the login node of a cluster (Slurm, PBS or LSF installed, outside a job), at most 4 threads: it is everyone's, and meant for editing and submitting jobs. Zeit warns once per process when it uses fewer threads for these reasons, and zeit doctor shows the users it counted; the results are the same, only the speed changes. n_jobs, ZEIT_NUM_THREADS or zeit config threads N set the count instead, and the last needs no environment variable (on Windows, a variable for the whole system needs an administrator).

With Dask, leave n_jobs alone. The blocks of a cube that run at once share the core's threads: there is one pool per thread count in a process, so four blocks with n_jobs=-1 on dask's threads scheduler still run on as many threads as the processors, not four times as many, and dividing them among the blocks only leaves processors idle (LandTrendr on 2048 × 2048 pixels of 40 years, blocks of 512, 20 processors: 4.3 s with -1, 10.1 s with 5 threads per block). In a distributed worker, -1 is the worker's threads (4 processes of 5 threads: 4.3 s, against 6.0 s with the nanny's single thread per block). One catch: creating a LocalCluster leaves OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 in the process that created it, so zeit run there outside Dask then uses one thread; ZEIT_NUM_THREADS or n_jobs sets it back.

On a node of 128 cores, a job of --cpus-per-task=16 gets 16 threads, without --jobs. Clusters' modules often export OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 (for MPI programs): zeit then warns once that it leaves the job's other processors idle, and ZEIT_NUM_THREADS, read first, sets zeit's count without touching the other programs'.

docs.title: doctor
docs.text:
zeit.doctor(network=True)

Prints what zeit finds on this computer: the threads of n_jobs=-1 and where the number comes from (16 threads (16 of 128 processors available to this process; Slurm job 123456)), the users with a session it divides them among, zeit config threads if set, the job and array task it runs in, the caches and whether they can be written, whether the services zeit downloads from answer (STAC, Earth Engine, Hugging Face, the embeddings), the Earth Engine credentials and the versions. The same as zeit doctor in a terminal: the first thing to run on a new cluster, and to paste in an issue.

Parameter Type Default Description network bool True Check the services (a few seconds without internet access).

docs.title: fetch_tiles
docs.text:
zeit.fetch_tiles(inputs, *, cache_dir=None, threads=4, verbose=True)

Downloads or builds the tiles of inputs (tile_urls, stac_tiles, gee_tiles, or a .txt file of URLs) into the tile cache, where run_tiles looks for them before fetching them itself. On a cluster, run it on the login node, which has internet access, with ZEIT_CACHE_DIR set to a folder the compute nodes also see: they then process the tiles without it. The same as zeit fetch tiles.

Parameter Type Default Description inputs recipes or path The tiles. A folder of tiles is already on disk, so it is refused. cache_dir path None Where to keep them (default: the tiles folder of the cache). threads int 4 Tiles fetched at once. verbose bool True Print each tile as it arrives.

Returns the cached files. A tile that cannot be fetched does not stop the others: a RuntimeError at the end lists those that failed.

docs.title: fetch_weights
docs.text:
zeit.fetch_weights(*names)

Downloads the pretrained weights of zeit.ai into the cache, checked by SHA-256, without importing torch: "presto", "prithvi-tiny-tl", "prithvi-100m-tl", "prithvi-300m", "prithvi-300m-tl", "prithvi-600m", "prithvi-600m-tl", or "all" (also with no names). Returns the files. The same as zeit fetch weights.

docs.title: Visualisation
docs.text:
One function to look at any Zeit data or result: a map, a time-series cube, a LandTrendr, CCDC, BFAST or Mann-Kendall result, or one pixel's series. In a notebook it is an interactive viewer that pages through dense time series at the display's frame rate; elsewhere it opens the same viewer in its own window, or draws a matplotlib figure for a report.

Install

zeit.plot needs the plot extra: pip install zeit-cdts[plot] (matplotlib and anywidget). Install pywebview too if you want a native window outside the notebook instead of a browser tab. import zeit does not load any of them; they are imported the first time you plot.

docs.title: plot
docs.text:
zeit.plot(
    data, *, var=None, time=None, band=None, rgb=None, kind=None,
    cmap=None, vmin=None, vmax=None, classes=None, nodata="auto",
    title=None, static=None, ax=None, figsize=None, colorbar=True,
    ncols=4, max_size=None, save=None, height=480, fps=8,
    compress=True, fit=None, pixel=None, basemap=None, vector=None,
    opacity=None, vector_color="#ffd400", block=None,
)

Shows data in the most useful form for where you are. All parameters but data are keyword-only, and every colour choice is inferred from the data (see Colours) but can be overridden. Tutorial: Plotting and Exploring Results.

Where you are What zeit.plot returns A notebook: JupyterLab, Notebook 7, VS Code notebooks, Colab An interactive viewer widget (anywidget), shown as the cell's output A script or a terminal, on a machine with a screen The same viewer in its own window: a native window with pywebview, otherwise a browser tab. In a script the call blocks until the window is closed, like plt.show() static=True, save= given, or no screen (no display, CI, tests, or the environment variable ZEIT_PLOT=static) A matplotlib Figure One pixel's series, or pixel= Always a matplotlib Figure

data can be:

Input Example Shown as A (time, y, x) or (time, band, y, x) cube, numpy- or dask-backed zeit.load_raster("LT_Stack_NDVI_Rondonia.tif") One frame per date. With band=, one band; a cube with red, green and blue bands is shown in colour A map (y, x): DataArray or numpy loss.yod One map A raster path, read lazily "LT_Stack_NDVI_Rondonia.tif" As the cube load_raster reads A result Dataset zeit.landtrendr(ndvi), zeit.extract_events(lt), zeit.ccdc(cube), zeit.mann_kendall(ndvi) One variable (var=, default the first map); the viewer has a selector for the others One pixel's series: a 1-D DataArray or a pandas.Series ndvi.sel(x=-63.2, y=-10.21, method="nearest") A line plot (always static)

Every dimension other than y and x becomes a frame axis, so the same viewer pages through dates, LandTrendr's vertices or CCDC's segments and coefficients. Frames are labelled the way save_raster names bands: 1985 for annual dates, 2020-01-15 otherwise, 3 for the third vertex, 1_blue_a0 for one CCDC coefficient (segment, band, coefficient).

Parameter Type Default Description data DataArray, Dataset, ndarray, dask array, path or pd.Series required What to show (see the table above). var str None Variable of a Dataset to show. Default: the first one with y and x dims. time int, str, date or list None Static plots: the frames to draw. An index (0, -1), a label ("2015"), a year (2015) or date ("2015-07-01", nearest), a list of these, or "all". Default: up to 12 frames spread over the series. The viewer always shows every frame. band str or int None Band to show from a (time, band, y, x) cube (a label of its band coordinate). A cube of embeddings is shown through its principal components, or in the viewer's embedding views; band= shows one dimension instead. rgb bool None Show the red, green and blue bands as a colour image. Default: when the band axis has them (red/green/blue, r/g/b, B04/B03/B02, SR_B4/SR_B3/SR_B2). False shows one band at a time. kind str None How to colour: "continuous", "diverging", "categorical", "years" or "rgb". Default: inferred (see Colours). cmap str None Any matplotlib colormap name. Default: depends on kind. vmin float None Lower colour limit. Default: the 2nd percentile of a sample. vmax float None Upper colour limit. Default: the 98th percentile of a sample. classes list or dict None Categories: a list of values, or {value: label} / {value: (label, colour)}. Values not listed are not drawn. nodata "auto", float or None "auto" Value drawn transparent, besides NaN. "auto": the raster's NoData; for integer maps without one that are not categories, 0 (Earth Engine exports, LandTrendr's yod). A number: that value. None: only NaN. title str None Title of the figure or viewer. Default: the variable's name (in a static plot, only for a single map). static bool None True: a matplotlib figure. False: the interactive viewer. Default: the viewer, unless save is given or there is no screen (see above). ax matplotlib Axes None Static plots: draw one map into this axes (pick one frame with time=). figsize tuple None Static plots: figure size in inches. Default: from the number of maps and their aspect. colorbar bool True Static plots: draw the colour bar or the class legend. ncols int 4 Static plots: maps per row in a grid of frames. max_size int None Longest side, in cells, that maps are read at: 1024 for static plots, 800 for the viewer's preview (finer cells are fetched when you zoom in). The cube is never read at full resolution as a whole. save str None Write the figure to this file (PNG, PDF, SVG…, at 150 dpi) and return it. Makes the plot static unless static=False. height int 480 Viewer in a notebook: height of the map in pixels. The window version fills its window. fps int 8 Viewer: playback speed, in frames per second. Can be changed in the viewer. compress bool True Viewer: send frames deflate-compressed. Smaller transfers for remote notebooks, at a little work on each side. fit Dataset None A result on the same grid, from landtrendr, ccdc, extract_events, bfast_monitor, bfast_lite, bfast or mann_kendall. Clicking a pixel in the viewer (or pixel=) shows its series with what the algorithm made of it. Matched to the data by coordinates. pixel (x, y) None A point in the data's coordinates: plot that pixel's series (with fit's overlays) as a figure, instead of maps. basemap str or xyzservices provider None A web map under the data: "satellite" (Esri World Imagery), "osm", "light" / "dark" (Esri grey canvases), "topo" (OpenTopoMap), an xyzservices provider or its name ("Esri.WorldImagery"), or a {z}/{x}/{y} URL template. The data needs a CRS, any CRS. vector path, GeoDataFrame, GeoSeries or shapely geometry None Outlines drawn over the maps: a vector file, a GeoDataFrame or GeoSeries, a shapely geometry or a list of them. Reprojected to the data's CRS. opacity float None Opacity of the data, 0–1. Default: 1, or 0.8 over a basemap. The viewer has a slider. vector_color str "#ffd400" Colour of the outlines. block bool None Window outside a notebook: wait until it is closed. Default: yes when running a script, no in an interactive interpreter (python -i, IPython), where the window stays open until close() or the interpreter exits.

Returns

  • a matplotlib.figure.Figure for a static plot (save= also writes it);
  • the viewer widget in a notebook. It shows itself as the cell's output; assign it (v = zeit.plot(...)) and put v on a line of its own to show it later;
  • a Window outside a notebook, with url (the page's address on 127.0.0.1, including its access token), close() and wait(). It is also a context manager.

docs.title: The viewer
docs.text:
The viewer sends each frame once to the browser as one byte per cell (a colour index), and the browser's GPU paints it through a 256-colour lookup table (WebGL2). Frames are preloaded from the current one outwards, so once they have arrived, paging through time does not involve Python at all. It runs at the display's refresh rate, and keeps working while another cell runs.

To Do Pan Drag the map. Zoom Mouse wheel, around the cursor. When you stop (and playback is paused), the visible window is fetched again at a finer resolution, down to full resolution. Reset the view Double-click. Play or pause Space, or the ▶ button. Step through frames ← and →, Home and End for the first and last frame, or drag the slider. Change the speed The fps selector (1 to 60 frames per second). Read a value Hover: the frame, the coordinates and the value under the cursor appear below the map. The value is read back from the colour index, so it is exact for categories and within 1/254 of the colour range otherwise (≈); values beyond vmin/vmax read as the limit. See a pixel's series Click a pixel: its full series appears below the map, with fit='s overlays. Click the chart to jump to that date. Show another variable The selector next to the title (Datasets). See the basemap through the data The opacity slider (with basemap=).

The keys work once the viewer has the focus: click it first.

What fit= draws over a pixel's series:

fit from Overlay landtrendr The fitted segments, with a marker at each vertex ccdc Each segment's harmonic model (for the band shown, or band=) and its break extract_events The event as a shaded span, from yod to yod + duration; for events of CCDC and BFAST, a line on the date of the break bfast_monitor The break, and where monitoring starts bfast_lite, bfast The breaks (trend and season breaks for bfast) mann_kendall The Theil-Sen line, labelled increasing, decreasing or no trend

The result is matched to the data by coordinates, so it may cover only part of the cube (a fit computed on a crop works on the whole map). A result without coordinates must have the data's shape.

docs.title: Embeddings
docs.text:
A cube of embeddings (load_embeddings) has 64 or 128 dimensions per pixel, with no physical unit: what matters is how vectors compare. For it the viewer sends the vectors themselves to the browser, each year once, as one byte per dimension (a scale per dimension, from the 0.1 and 99.9 % percentiles of a sample), and the GPU computes each view from them. Changing view, reference or year does not involve Python. A panel beside the map picks the view:

View What it shows Components (RGB) Three of the first six principal components as red, green and blue (PC1–3 by default), stretched between their 2 and 98 % percentiles, with the share of the variance each explains. Fitted on every year, so a colour means the same embedding in each year and playing the years shows change; or on the visible area, refitted when you stop panning or zooming, which spreads the colours over the differences on screen (the states of a forest rather than forest versus city). Similarity The cosine similarity of every pixel to a reference vector: the pixel under the cursor, live as the mouse moves, or a pinned pixel (click a pixel; click it again or press Esc to unpin). Keep the reference's year fixes the year the reference is taken from while you page through the others ("did this pasture come to look like the forest?"). Colours from the 2nd percentile of the similarity to 1. Change 1 − the cosine similarity of each pixel's vectors in the year shown and the previous year (or a year you pick). Colours from 0 to the 98th percentile.

Hovering reads the components, the similarity or the change under the cursor. The panel draws the latent profile, the values of the cursor's (and the pin's) vector along its dimensions, and the chart below the map follows the cursor: the similarity of its pixel (and the pin's) to the reference in every year.

To keep the browser's memory bounded, a year's vectors are at most 48 MB: a 500 × 500 cube of 128 dimensions (TESSERA) travels at full resolution, larger ones at coarser cells, and zooming in fetches the visible window at finer cells, as for any cube. Measured on a 500 × 500 × 128 cube (2026-10-10, Edge, a local window): the first year on screen in 1.2 s, four years in 3.7 s, and the similarity map redrawn about 30 ms after the mouse moves. A static plot (static=True) shows the components fitted on every year.

Outside a notebook, the viewer is served by a small HTTP server on 127.0.0.1 under a random token, so other users of the machine and other web pages cannot read the data. The server stops when the window is closed, when you call close(), or when Python exits.

docs.title: Colours
docs.text:
Colours are chosen from a sample of the data (a few frames, decimated), never from the whole cube:

The data kind Palette Legend A band axis with red, green and blue "rgb" 2–98 % stretch shared by the three bands none bool, classes= given, or integers with at most 32 distinct values (not years) "categorical" One colour per value (tab10, then tab20) Class legend Years: a name such as yod, year or *_year, dates (datetime64, e.g. CCDC's t_break), or integers all between 1800 and 2200 "years" plasma Whole-year ticks Values on both sides of 0 in comparable amounts (the smaller side at least 20 % of the larger) "diverging" RdBu, symmetric around 0 Colour bar Anything else "continuous" viridis, or RdYlGn (green high) when the name contains a vegetation index (NDVI, EVI, SAVI, NBR, NDMI, NDWI, …) Colour bar, limits at the 2nd and 98th percentiles

NaN and NoData (see nodata) are transparent, so a basemap or the page shows through. load_raster names a cube after its file, so LT_Stack_NDVI_Rondonia.tif gets the vegetation palette. A float map with a few values, such as Mann-Kendall's trend (−1, 0, 1), counts as continuous; give it classes= to get a legend.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
import zeit

ndvi = zeit.load_raster("LT_Stack_NDVI_Rondonia.tif")   # (time, y, x), 1985-2024

# In a notebook: the interactive viewer. Drag, wheel, space to play.
zeit.plot(ndvi)

# A static grid of years, written to a file
zeit.plot(ndvi, time=["1985", "2000", "2015", "2024"], save="ndvi_years.png")

# A result Dataset: the viewer has a selector for its variables
lt = zeit.landtrendr(ndvi)
loss = zeit.extract_events(lt, min_magnitude=2000)
zeit.plot(loss)                                   # yod first, with year ticks
zeit.plot(loss, var="magnitude", static=True)     # one variable as a figure

# Click a pixel to see its series and LandTrendr's fit
zeit.plot(ndvi, fit=lt)

# The same as a figure, for one pixel (x, y in the data's CRS)
zeit.plot(ndvi, fit=lt, pixel=(-63.2001, -10.2116), static=True)

# Over satellite imagery, with an area of interest
zeit.plot(loss.yod, basemap="satellite", vector="aoi.gpkg", opacity=0.7)

# Categories with your own labels and colours
mk = zeit.mann_kendall(ndvi)
zeit.plot(mk, var="trend", classes={-1: ("decreasing", "#d62728"), 0: ("no trend", "#dddddd"),
                                    1: ("increasing", "#2ca02c")})

# Into your own matplotlib layout
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
fig, (a, b) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10, 4))
zeit.plot(ndvi, time="1985", ax=a, static=True)
zeit.plot(ndvi, time="2024", ax=b, static=True)

In a script, the viewer opens in its own window and the script waits until you close it:

# look.py: run with `python look.py`
import zeit

ndvi = zeit.load_raster("LT_Stack_NDVI_Rondonia.tif")
lt = zeit.landtrendr(ndvi)
zeit.plot(ndvi, fit=lt)        # opens a window; returns when it is closed

In an interactive interpreter the call returns at once and the window stays open:

>>> w = zeit.plot(ndvi)
>>> w.url
'http://127.0.0.1:52113/Qm3n.../'
>>> w.close()

Outside a notebook, set ZEIT_PLOT=static in the environment to get figures instead of windows, for example for batch jobs that render reports.

docs.title: Post-processing
docs.text: Clean up maps, classify CCDC results and derive masks.

docs.title: Spatial filters
docs.text: The filters take a map (a DataArray, a numpy array or a raster path) and give back the same kind, georeferencing, NoData and attributes kept.

docs.title: apply_mmu_filter
docs.text:
zeit.spatial.apply_mmu_filter(data, mmu_pixels=11, *, nodata="auto")

Minimum mapping unit filter: connected (4-neighbour) patches of pixels holding a value, whatever the value, smaller than mmu_pixels become NoData. Removes the salt-and-pepper noise of per-pixel change maps (a LandTrendr year of loss, a magnitude). Also exported as zeit.apply_mmu_filter; CLI: zeit mmu-filter.

Parameter Type Default Description data DataArray, ndarray or path required A single map, e.g. a year-of-loss map. mmu_pixels int 11 Smallest patch to keep, in pixels (11 Landsat pixels ≈ 1 ha). nodata "auto" or float "auto" The value of "no feature": the map's NoData, else 0 (NaN for floats with NaN). 
loss = zeit.extract_events(lt, min_magnitude=1500)
yod = zeit.apply_mmu_filter(loss.yod, mmu_pixels=11)
zeit.save_raster(yod, "results/loss_year_mmu.tif")

docs.title: apply_majority_filter
docs.text:
zeit.spatial.apply_majority_filter(
    image, size=3, *, iterations=1, nodata="auto", n_jobs=-1,
)

Majority (mode) filter: each pixel of a class map takes the most common class of its window (cut at the edges), its own when it is among the most common (else the smallest of them), iterations times or until nothing changes. NoData pixels stay and do not vote. Also exported as zeit.apply_majority_filter.

Parameter Type Default Description image DataArray, ndarray or path required 2-D class map. size int 3 Window size, odd (3 = 3 × 3). iterations int 1 How many times to apply it. nodata "auto", float or None "auto" The map's NoData (NaN for floats), a number, or none. n_jobs int -1 Threads.

docs.title: mmu_sieve
docs.text:
zeit.spatial.mmu_sieve(
    data, min_size=11, *, connectivity=8, nodata="auto",
)

Minimum mapping unit of a class map by a sieve: each patch (pixels of one class connected 4- or 8-wise) of fewer than min_size pixels is merged, the smallest first, into the neighbouring patch with which it shares the longest border (on a tie, the largest), and takes its class; a merge that joins patches of one class makes a single patch of them. Unlike apply_mmu_filter, the map stays complete (as with GDAL's sieve): the small patches take a class, they are not emptied. A patch surrounded only by NoData stays. Also exported as zeit.mmu_sieve.

Parameter Type Default Description data DataArray, ndarray or path required 2-D class map. min_size int 11 Patches with fewer pixels are merged (11 Landsat pixels ≈ 1 ha). connectivity int 8 4 or 8: diagonal pixels in the same patch. nodata "auto", float or None "auto" The map's NoData (NaN for floats), a number, or none.

docs.title: apply_bayesian_filter
docs.text:
zeit.spatial.apply_bayesian_filter(probs, window_size=3)

Smooths per-class probabilities spatially, then takes the most likely class. Unlike the majority filter, confident pixels resist being overruled by their neighbours. Import from zeit.spatial.

Parameter Type Default Description probs DataArray or ndarray required (class, y, x) probabilities or scores, e.g. zeit.classify(..., probability=True).probability. window_size int 3 Averaging window.

Returns the winning class per pixel (y, x): its index for a numpy array, the class itself for a DataArray whose first dim has coordinates.

docs.title: smooth_probs
docs.text:
zeit.spatial.smooth_probs(
    probs, window_size=9, neigh_fraction=0.5, smoothness=20.0, *,
    n_jobs=-1,
)

Bayesian smoothing of class probabilities, after Camara et al. (2024, Remote Sensing 16(23):4572), written from the paper. Each class's logit, log(p / (sum - p)), is pulled towards the mean m of the highest neigh_fraction of the logits of its window (mirrored at the edges), the more the less that neighbourhood varies (s²) against smoothness: w = s² / (s² + smoothness), x' = w x + (1 - w) m. A pixel whose model is confident keeps its class against consistent neighbours, while the noise among uncertain pixels goes. The result agrees with bayesEO's bayes_smooth to about 2e-3, with the same class everywhere in the tests (tests/test_postproc.py); a missing pixel stays missing and is left out of its neighbours'. Also exported as zeit.smooth_probs.
