No third-party code was used, and the formulas were written from the literature as recalled, without the papers at hand; they were checked by their properties, by Wald's protocol on synthetic scenes and on a CBERS-4A WPM and a Landsat 8 window and, for the Brovey, against GDAL's output. The defaults of "hpf" are zeit's and not Gangkofner et al.'s: the kernel and the regression gain were chosen on those two real windows, so treat them as a starting point.

Grids. The CRS must be the same (nothing is reprojected), the grids north-up, the pan's cells finer and the footprints overlapping; the ratio comes from the cell sizes (the geometric mean over x and y; ratio= overrides it). The corners need not coincide: the warp puts the bands on the pan's cells at any offset. What that does to the statistics: the pan reduced to the bands' resolution for the regression (a box filter of side 2 floor(ratio / 2) + 1 sampled every round(ratio) pixels) is then taken at the pan pixel nearest each cell's centre, off by up to half a pixel, which the filter's width hides; with whole blocks the reduction would be the cell's exact mean. A ratio that is not whole rounds the filter and the HPF kernel. Pan cells outside the bands' footprint are NaN. The registration of the pan to the bands (geolocation) is not checked or corrected: use coregister first.

Missing data. A pixel that is NaN (or nodata) in the pan or in any band is NaN in the output and out of every statistic (the regression, means, variances and principal components; per date, over the whole scene); a missing cell of a band makes the pan cells it covers NaN.

Parameter Type Default Description ms DataArray required (time, band, y, x) or (band, y, x) with a CRS. In memory (a lazy cube is computed). pan DataArray required (y, x) (or one band) on the finer grid, or (time, y, x) matching ms's dates. method str "gsa" "gsa", "brovey", "hpf" or "pca". ratio float None Pan cells per band cell, when it must differ from the ratio of the cell sizes. weights sequence or dict None "brovey": the weights of the intensity (in the bands' order, or by label; normalised to sum 1). Default: fitted. intensity_bands list None "gsa", "pca", fitted "brovey": the bands (labels or positions) that enter the estimate of the intensity. Default: all. kernel int None "hpf": the odd side of the box filter in pan pixels; 2 floor(ratio / 2) + 1 by default. gain float or "regression" "regression" "hpf": each band's regression slope on the low-passed pan, or a number: the weight of the paper's modulation (1.0 is Gangkofner's). nodata "auto", float or None "auto" Missing values besides NaN, in both inputs: the raster's NoData (0 for integer data without one), a number or None. n_jobs int -1 Threads (the processors zeit may use by default). The output does not depend on it.

Returns float32, the bands of ms on the pan's grid, with the coordinates, CRS and attributes of ms (attrs["pansharpen"] says the method and the ratio). Everything is in memory: a 10,000 x 10,000 pan with four bands is 1.6 GB of output plus the resampled bands. A whole scene larger than that (a WPM scene is about 46,000 pixels across) needs tiles with a margin for the cubic resampling and the HPF's kernel, and the statistics of the whole scene computed beforehand and handed to the tiles.

fused = zeit.pansharpen(wpm_ms, wpm_pan, method="gsa")                       # CBERS-4A WPM, ratio 4
fused = zeit.pansharpen(l8_ms, l8_b8, "gsa", intensity_bands=["B3", "B4"])   # Landsat 8: the pan sees green and red

docs.title: coregister
docs.text:
zeit.coregister(
    cube, reference, *, window_size=256, window_position=None, max_shift=5, max_iter=5,
    band=None, ref_band=None, resampling="cubic", nodata="auto", min_reliability=None, n_jobs=-1,
)

Moves each date of a cube to fit a reference image: the global co-registration of AROSICS (Scheffler et al. 2017, Remote Sensing 9(7):676; COREG of AROSICS 1.14.0, Apache-2.0, Daniel Scheffler, GFZ Potsdam), ported to the compiled core (rust/zeit-core/src/coreg.rs, which Janus links directly). For each date, one band is matched to the reference's by the phase correlation of a window at the centre of what the two images have in common: the cross power spectrum F0 conj(F1) / (|F0| |F1|) of the two windows (single-precision FFTs of the largest power of 2 inside the window), whose peak is their shift in whole pixels and whose side maxima give the part of a pixel. The integer shift is checked by moving the reference's window by it and correlating again (up to max_iter times); a shift above max_shift pixels, or with no clear match, is a failure. Every band of the date is then moved by the shift with the warp kernel of load_raster(..., like=) (GDAL's resampling, resampling="cubic" by default) onto the cube's own grid; a shift of a whole number of pixels is a plain copy of the cells.

The cube and the reference must be on the same pixel grid (the same projected CRS, the same cell size, the cells a whole number apart; their extents may differ and only what they share is matched). Where AROSICS resamples the window of the other image when the grids differ, coregister asks for the reference to be put on the cube's grid first (zeit.load_raster(..., like=cube)), and says so in the error.

Parameter Type Default Description cube DataArray required (time, band, y, x), (band, y, x), (time, y, x) or (y, x) in a projected CRS. A lazy cube is read a date at a time and the result is lazy. reference DataArray required (band, y, x) or (y, x) in the same CRS, on the same pixel grid. window_size int 256 The matching window's side in pixels (AROSICS' ws). It is cut down to the overlap, and the FFT takes the largest power of 2 inside it. window_position (x, y) None The window's centre in map coordinates (AROSICS' wp); by default the centroid of the overlap of the valid data. max_shift float 5 The largest shift accepted, in pixels. max_iter int 5 Tries to validate the integer shift. band, ref_band label or position None The band of the cube and of the reference to match (the first by default). resampling str "cubic" The resampling that moves the images (those of load_raster: "cubic", "bilinear", "nearest", "lanczos"...). nodata "auto", number, None or (reference, cube) "auto" Missing values besides NaN: each image's raster NoData, a number for both, None, or a pair. min_reliability float None Treats a shift whose reliability (AROSICS', 0-100) is below this as not found. None takes every shift AROSICS' checks accept, as its COREG does. n_jobs int -1 Dates run at once (the processors zeit may use by default); each date's correlation is one thread.

Returns (aligned, shifts). aligned is the cube on its own grid with each date moved by its shift; the dates that failed are as they were. shifts is a pandas.DataFrame, one row per date (index time; one row for a cube without dates), with x_shift_px and y_shift_px (pixels: the amount the date was moved, x to the right and y down, AROSICS' convention), x_shift_map and y_shift_map (map units; y is negative for a shift down on a north-up grid), reliability (0-100), ssim_before and ssim_after (structural similarity of the window to the reference's before and after the shift), success, reason (why it failed), the matching window window_x0, window_y0, window_x1, window_y1 (cells of the cube, [x0, x1)), fft_size (the side of the FFT window of the spectrum the shift is read from: after an integer shift the reference's window is moved by it and shrinks, so it is smaller than the matching window's largest power of 2) and applied.

aligned, shifts = zeit.coregister(cube, reference, band="nir", ref_band="nir")
shifts[["x_shift_px", "y_shift_px", "reliability", "ssim_before", "ssim_after", "success"]]
good = aligned.sel(time=shifts.index[shifts.success])

A date that fails stays as it was. No valid data in common, an overlap of 16 x 16 pixels or less, a window that cannot be placed on valid data, no integer shift that survives the check in max_iter tries, or a shift above max_shift (AROSICS raises these as errors; here they are success=False with the reason). A featureless date (constant) fails that way. AROSICS itself applies any shift that passes those checks, however low its reliability or similarity (its local variant filters tie points by them); min_reliability is Zeit's option to refuse the weak ones, and ssim_before and ssim_after are there to check that the window agrees better afterwards.

Where it differs from AROSICS. The numbers are AROSICS' (see below); the plumbing is not:

  • The overlap is that of the two images' valid pixels (not NaN, not NoData), and the window is placed on it as AROSICS places it on the intersection of the footprint polygons: the centroid, clipped to the overlap, moved to the grid by the floor of its edges, and cut down by one pixel a side when AROSICS' other window does not fit, as it does in an image smaller than the window. AROSICS fills the holes of a footprint, so a cloud masked as NaN is inside its window; here the window is grown from its centre until it meets the hole (as AROSICS grows it where its footprint polygon has an edge), or fails when nothing of 16 x 16 pixels is left.
  • The aligned images are resampled onto the cube's grid; AROSICS with align_grids=False only moves the origin of the geotransform. Zeit's grid stays the cube's, which is what a time series needs.
  • The window's values are float32 (AROSICS reads the file's type and converts to single precision for the FFT; the similarity of an integer image rounds and clamps the shifted window to the type as GDAL does).
  • In AROSICS' retry loop, a shift found by a retry gets (0, 0) as its integer part (a quirk of calculate_spatial_shifts); it is kept, since the shifts are meant to be AROSICS'.
  • This is the global variant; the local one, with a grid of tie points and a warp fitted to them, is coregister_local.

Agreement with AROSICS 1.14.0. On 13 pairs (12 synthetic and a natural image; the two where neither finds a shift fail alike), the shifts differ from AROSICS' by 2e-7 pixels at most (the single-precision noise of two FFT libraries); the integer part, the window, the FFT size and the reliability are equal; the similarity too on the synthetic pairs; and the two aligned images differ by one unit of float32 (see Against the Original Implementations).

docs.title: coregister_local
docs.text:
zeit.coregister_local(
    cube, reference, *, grid_res=200, window_size=(256, 256), max_shift=5, max_iter=5,
    min_reliability=60, tie_point_filter_level=3, rs_max_outlier=10, rs_tolerance=2.5,
    rs_random_state=0, warp="auto", order=None, min_points=5, band=None, ref_band=None,
    resampling="cubic", nodata="auto", arosics_compat=False, n_jobs=-1,
)

Warps each date of a cube to fit a reference image by shifts that vary across the scene: the local co-registration of AROSICS (COREG_LOCAL of AROSICS 1.14.0, Apache-2.0, Daniel Scheffler, GFZ Potsdam; Scheffler et al. 2017, Remote Sensing 9(7):676), ported to the compiled core (rust/zeit-core/src/coreg_local.rs, with the matching of coregister for each point). A grid of tie points is laid over the image, every grid_res pixels from the corner (AROSICS' own grid: 0, grid_res, 2 * grid_res, ... up to one step past the image); each point on data of both images is matched with a window of window_size pixels centred on it, which gives the shift there, its reliability and the structural similarity of the window before and after. The points are then filtered in AROSICS' order: level 1, a reliability below min_reliability; level 2, a window that is less similar to the reference's after the shift; level 3, RANSAC: scikit-image's ransac of an affine model of the shifts, with 6 samples, up to 2000 trials and a residual threshold that AROSICS searches (in map units) until the outliers are rs_max_outlier percent plus or minus rs_tolerance. The points that remain are control points: each date is warped onto the cube's grid by GDAL (through rasterio) from them, with a thin plate spline, which AROSICS always uses (warp="tps", what "auto" is), or a polynomial (warp="polynomial", GDAL's choice of order from the number of points or an order of 1 to 3). It corrects what a single shift cannot: a misregistration that grows across the scene, a bad orthorectification, a viewing-geometry effect.

As in coregister, the cube and the reference must be on the same pixel grid and the overlap is that of the valid pixels (NaN, NoData); the points are on the cube's own pixel corners.

Parameter Type Default Description cube DataArray required (time, band, y, x), (band, y, x), (time, y, x) or (y, x) in a projected CRS. A lazy cube is read a date at a time; the result is in memory. reference DataArray required (band, y, x) or (y, x) in the same CRS, on the same pixel grid. grid_res float 200 The spacing of the tie points in pixels (AROSICS' grid_res). window_size int or (x, y) (256, 256) The matching window's side in pixels; a pair must be of equal values (the window is square). max_shift, max_iter float, int 5, 5 As in coregister, for each point. min_reliability float 60 Tie points below this reliability (0-100) are flagged (level 1). tie_point_filter_level int 3 AROSICS' tieP_filter_level: 0 none, 1 reliability, 2 plus the similarity, 3 plus RANSAC. rs_max_outlier, rs_tolerance float 10, 2.5 RANSAC's expected outliers and the tolerance of that, in percent. rs_random_state int or None 0 RANSAC's seed (AROSICS' rs_random_state); None takes one from the clock. With the same seed the flags are AROSICS'. warp str "auto" "tps" (GDAL's thin plate spline), "polynomial", or "auto" ("tps", as AROSICS). order int None The polynomial's order, 1 to 3 (warp="polynomial"); None lets GDAL choose from the number of points. min_points int 5 A date with fewer control points (AROSICS' min_points_local_corr) is left as it was and flagged. band, ref_band label or position None The band of the cube and of the reference to match (the first by default); every band of a date is warped with the same points. resampling str "cubic" The resampling of the warp ("cubic", "bilinear", "nearest", "lanczos"...). nodata "auto", number, None or (reference, cube) "auto" Missing values besides NaN: each image's raster NoData, a number for both, None, or a pair. arosics_compat bool False Reproduces a bug of AROSICS 1.14.0 in the RANSAC flags (below), to compare with it. n_jobs int -1 Threads (the processors zeit may use by default): the points of each date, and the dates, run on them.

Returns (aligned, tie_points). aligned is the cube on its own grid with each date warped (the dates with fewer than min_points control points as they were). tie_points is a pandas.DataFrame with a row for every tie point of every date: time, point_id (the position in the whole grid, AROSICS' POINT_ID), col and row (the corner of the cube's pixels), x and y (map), x_shift_px and y_shift_px, x_shift_map and y_shift_map (the amount the date has to be moved there, x to the right and y down, as in coregister; NaN where the match failed), abs_shift (map units) and angle (degrees from north), reliability, ssim_before, ssim_after and ssim_improved, success and reason, win_size_x and win_size_y, fft_size, the flags of the filters outlier_reliability, outlier_ssim and outlier_ransac and their union outlier, used (the point is a control point) and date_applied. tie_points.attrs["dates"] is a table with one row per date: the points placed, matched and used, whether the date was warped, and why not.

aligned, points = zeit.coregister_local(cube, reference, grid_res=100, window_size=128, band="nir", ref_band="nir")
points[points.used][["time", "x", "y", "x_shift_map", "y_shift_map"]]
points.attrs["dates"]

A point or a date that fails is flagged, not raised. A point whose window cannot be placed on data, with no clear match or a shift above max_shift has success=False and a reason; a date with too few control points is returned as it was (date_applied=False; AROSICS in that case corrects with the mean shift of the points, Zeit leaves the date alone, since a global shift is coregister's job). A date with more than 7000 control points is warped from 7000 evenly spaced ones (AROSICS draws them at random: a limit of GDAL's spline).

Where it differs from AROSICS.

  • As in coregister, the overlap is the valid pixels, not the footprint polygons. A window that touches a diagonal edge or a hole is grown from the point until it meets the no-data pixels, as AROSICS grows it inside its polygon; the same windows on the benchmark's pairs, which have a diagonal edge.
  • RANSAC's flags are put on their points; AROSICS 1.14.0 puts them on others. When the reliability or similarity filter has flagged points, AROSICS gives the flags of RANSAC (one for each point RANSAC got) to the table's rows by their labels instead of their positions (inGDF['outliers'] = outliers in _RANSAC_outlier_detection), so the flags land on the wrong points: real outliers stay and as many good points are dropped. Zeit's default flags the points RANSAC found. arosics_compat=True reproduces AROSICS' assignment, which is how the comparison below is exact.
  • RANSAC is scikit-image's, with numpy's random generator (PCG64 seeded by a SeedSequence, Generator.choice without replacement) reproduced in the core, so the samples, the inliers at every threshold and the flags are AROSICS'. The time limit of the threshold search (rs_timeout, 20 s of clock) is not kept; with 5 or 6 points left for RANSAC (where AROSICS raises or returns nothing) none is flagged.
  • The warp is GDAL's, as AROSICS' (rasterio's reproject with the control points, SRC_METHOD=GCP_TPS), onto the cube's own grid.
  • Points run on threads of the core where AROSICS starts a process for each.

Agreement with AROSICS 1.14.0. On 7 pairs (6 synthetic and the camera image warped by a field; 19 to 165 points each), the points of the grid that are placed are the same, and so are the successes; the shifts differ from AROSICS' by 2e-6 pixels at most (2e-3 at one point of the natural image), the windows are equal, the reliability agrees to 8e-5 and the similarity before to 4e-8 and after to 2e-5 (3e-4 in the 8-bit image); the flags of the three filters are identical with arosics_compat=True; and the warped image, from the same control points, differs by 0.001 at most in float32 (by 1 in uint16), the 8-bit image by up to 6 in 0.01% of the cells (see Against the Original Implementations).

docs.title: level2
docs.text:
zeit.level2(
    safe, dem=None, *, brdf=True, topography=True, aod=True, adjacency=True,
    multiple_scattering=True, erase_cloud=False, flags=None, fmask=True, gswo=None,
    fmask_compat=False, dem_resampling="bilinear", n_jobs=8, merge=None,
    reference=None, coreg_band="BROADNIR", coreg_ref_band=None,
)

The atmospheric correction of a Sentinel-2 Level 1C scene to surface reflectance, on a local .SAFE directory, or on the name of a product that it downloads first (download_l1c): what FORCE 3.11.00's force-l2ps does for one image (Frantz 2019, Remote Sensing 11:1124; David Frantz, GPL-3.0-or-later), in the Zeit core. The water vapour and the gases, the aerosol optical depth estimated from dark targets, the adjacency effect, the topographic and the BRDF corrections, and the products on the 10 m grid of the scene. The cloud, shadow, snow and water flags come from Zeit's own port of Fmask 4.7 (Qiu, Zhu and Woodcock 2019, Remote Sensing of Environment 231:111205; run at 20 m, with the DEM and optionally the GSWO), unless flags gives them or fmask=False. The 13 band files are read by GDAL (the product's JPEG 2000 or GeoTIFFs of the same names).

Parameter Type Default Description safe path or str required The .SAFE directory of a Level 1C product (MTD_MSIL1C.xml and one GRANULE/<name>/ with its IMG_DATA), or the name of a product (a string that is not an existing directory and ends with .SAFE or starts with S2, such as the product column of find_l1c): it is downloaded to the l1c cache by download_l1c. dem path, DataArray or "glo30" None The DEM in metres, any grid and CRS: it is put on the 10 m grid of the scene (dem_resampling). "glo30" makes the Copernicus GLO-30 DEM of the scene with download_dem. Needed for topography=True, and used by the atmosphere (elevation) and by the Fmask when given. brdf bool True Normalise the BRDF to nadir view and the sun at the zenith of the scene (FORCE's DO_BRDF). topography bool True The topographic correction of the illumination (DO_TOPO). Without dem it is a ValueError that says to pass the DEM or use topography=False. aod bool True Estimate the aerosol optical depth from the dark targets of the scene (DO_AOD); False uses the fallback spectrum. adjacency bool True The environmental weighting of the adjacency effect (ADJACENCY_EFFECT). multiple_scattering bool True Multiple scattering (MULTI_SCATTERING); False is single scattering. erase_cloud bool False Set the cloud pixels to no data (ERASE_CLOUD). flags ndarray or None None The cloud, shadow, snow and water bits of the QAI, int16 (nrows, ncols) on the 10 m grid. With them the Fmask does not run. fmask bool True Run Zeit's Fmask when flags is None. False runs no cloud detection: there is no cloud flag, and dst is 32767 in the whole image. gswo path or DataArray None Global Surface Water Occurrence (percent) for the Fmask, put on the 20 m grid by nearest neighbour. fmask_compat bool False True reproduces three oddities of the original Fmask 4.7 code; the default corrects them. dem_resampling str "bilinear" The resampling of the DEM onto the grid of the scene (FORCE's default). n_jobs int 8 Threads of the correction, the Fmask and the JPEG 2000 decoder. merge None, "regression" or "improphe" None FORCE's resolution merge (RES_MERGE): the red edge 1-3, B8A, SWIR1 and SWIR2 predicted at 10 m from green, red and the broad NIR (B08), the methods of sentinel2_resmerge with force=True (FORCE's arithmetic). It runs on the TOA reflectance, before the correction, as force-l2ps does; a pixel is predicted if it is not off and has no cloud and no shadow in the QAI (snow and water are predicted). reference path, DataArray or None None The image to coregister the scene to (any grid: it is put on the scene's with load_raster(..., like=)). The shift is found by coregister (AROSICS' global co-registration; FORCE's own coregistration is another method) on coreg_band of the TOA, and every band of the TOA and the QAI are moved by it, before the merge and the correction, so all the products come out aligned. coreg_band str "BROADNIR" The band of the scene that is matched: ULTRABLUE BLUE GREEN RED REDEDGE1 REDEDGE2 REDEDGE3 BROADNIR NIR VAPOR CIRRUS SWIR1 SWIR2 (BROADNIR is B08, NIR is B8A). coreg_ref_band label, position or None None The band of reference to match (the first by default).

Returns an xarray.Dataset on the grid of the scene (10 m, the CRS and the transform of the bands; x and y are the pixel centres): boa (band, y, x) int16, the reflectance times 10000 with _FillValue -9999 (band is BLUE, GREEN, RED, REDEDGE1, REDEDGE2, REDEDGE3, BROADNIR, NIR, SWIR1, SWIR2), and qai, dst, vzn, hot, aod, wvp (y, x) int16 in FORCE's units. attrs has datetime (UTC), sensor, baseline, aod_green (the optical depth of the scene in B03), aod_map (False when the fallback spectrum was used), water_vapor_cm (the mean of the wvp product), n_targets (valid water, shadow and vegetation dark targets), the summary of the Fmask as fmask_* keys (plain numbers, booleans and strings, so that it can be written to NetCDF), core_seconds and provenance; with merge, merge (the method); with reference, coreg_x_shift_px and coreg_y_shift_px (the amount the scene was moved, x to the right and y down, as in coregister), coreg_reliability (0-100), coreg_success and coreg_reason (empty on success). .zeit.save(path) writes one GeoTIFF per variable (a path with .tif, one multi-band file) and .zeit.plot() shows it.

What it is and what it is not, against FORCE. With FORCE's cloud flags, sun, geography and BRDF factor, boa (the 10 bands), qai, aod, wvp, hot, dst and vzn equal those of force-l2ps in 100 % of the pixels, on three runs of tile 23LKC (2023-07-28 without BRDF and with it, 2021-07-28 without BRDF; 120,560,400 pixels per band in 2023). With Zeit's own sun (a clean-room implementation) and FORCE's flags, 2023 without BRDF, 75 to 92 % of the pixels are equal band by band and the mean difference is 0.08 to 0.56 (reflectance times 10000). With Zeit's Fmask, its cloud or shadow mask agrees with FORCE's in 98.1 % of the pixels. The numbers are in the benchmark.

Merge and coregistration. Both are off by default and, like FORCE's resolution_merge and coregister, work on the TOA reflectance, after the cloud flags and before the radiometric correction, in that order (first the coregistration, then the merge): a merge or a shift applied to boa afterwards would not be FORCE's, because the aerosol, the vapour and the correction itself read the merged and shifted bands. They reach the core through a hook that level2_scene of the Rust core takes (a function of the TOA and the QAI called once, with the QAI as it is at that point: bounds, sun, topography and flags), so the Janus can use the same. The coregistration is coregister's, not FORCE's (FORCE's coregister is another method), so the shift is not compared with FORCE; if it is not found (coreg_success is False, coreg_reason says why) the scene is processed as it is. The topography, the geography and the sun do not move, as in FORCE. Pixels the shift uncovers, and pixels with no data in any band after the cubic, are off.

Agreement with FORCE for the merge. Tile 23LKC of 2023-07-28, without BRDF, with FORCE's cloud flags, sun, geography and BRDF factor as inputs (120,560,400 pixels per band; benchmarks/vs_originals/force_l2ps_real.py --merge). With "improphe", qai, dst, hot, aod, vzn and wvp equal FORCE's in every pixel and boa differs in 9 to 70 pixels per band (by 1 to 3). With "regression", FORCE's own result depends on its threads (it writes each prediction in place inside a parallel loop: against a run with 8 threads 4 to 8 % of the pixels of boa differ, and aod and wvp too); against a run with one thread, which is deterministic and has its own cloud mask, qai, dst, hot, aod, vzn and wvp are equal in every pixel, BLUE, GREEN, RED and BROADNIR are equal, and the six merged bands differ in 196 to 271 pixels each (by 2 to 12). Time of the merge alone on this scene with 8 threads: ImproPhe 11.4 s; regression 182 s with FORCE's arithmetic (force=True: in order, on one thread), 36 s without it. On a known shift (the BROADNIR of the scene moved by +2.5 pixels in x and -1.5 in y) the coregistration found +2.47 and -1.47, with a reliability of 95.6, and took 26 s more than the run without a reference.

Memory and time. Everything is in memory, on the whole scene at 10 m. On tile 23LKC (10980 x 10980, 8 threads, Zeit's Fmask, the GLO-30 DEM from a local file), the peak working set of the process was 21.6 GiB without the merge and 28.7 GiB with "improphe" or "regression", and the call took 146 s, 158 s and 332 s; the result itself is 3.6 GiB. A machine with 32 GB is short for the merge: give it more, or close other programs.

What it does not do. It does not search STAC itself (that is find_l1c), does not reproject to a datacube as FORCE does (the products stay on the 10 m grid of the scene), and is for Sentinel-2 only (Landsat is not in the public function). The scene without any cloud target gives dst 32767 in every pixel; that case was not compared with FORCE. The runs equal to FORCE used FORCE's cloud flags, sun, geography and BRDF factor as inputs; the public function computes them itself: Zeit's Fmask, Zeit's clean-room sun, the projection through GDAL/PROJ, and, for the BRDF, nbar's c-factor (Roy et al. 2016, 2017) in place of FORCE's brdf_factor (brdf-ll.c is not ported). The factor enters the AOD retrieval even with brdf=False. See the benchmark for what the differences cost.

l2 = zeit.level2("S2B_MSIL1C_20230728T132239_N0509_R038_T23LKC_20230728T150149.SAFE",
                 dem="cop_glo30_23LKC.tif", brdf=False)
red = l2.boa.sel(band="RED").where(l2.boa.sel(band="RED") != -9999) / 10000   # reflectance
l2.zeit.save("l2_20230728")                      # boa.tif, qai.tif, dst.tif, ... in a folder
l2 = zeit.level2(safe, brdf=False, topography=False)   # no DEM
l2 = zeit.level2("S2B_MSIL1C_20230728T132239_N0509_R038_T23LKC_20230728T150149.SAFE", dem="glo30")   # product and DEM downloaded

docs.title: find_l1c
docs.text:
zeit.find_l1c(
    tile=None, bbox=None, start=None, end=None, max_cloud=100.0,
    limit=None,
)

Searches the Sentinel-2 Level 1C products in the sentinel-2-l1c collection of Earth Search (STAC, with pystac-client), by MGRS tile or by box. Gives a table sorted by date whose product column is what download_l1c and level2 take.

Parameter Type Default Description tile str None MGRS tile, "23LKC" or "T23LKC" (the grid:code of the items). Exactly one of tile and bbox. bbox 4 numbers None (lon_min, lat_min, lon_max, lat_max) in degrees. start, end date None The interval, as "2023-07-28", a date or a datetime; a bare end date includes its whole day. Either one may be omitted. max_cloud float 100.0 Largest cloud cover, in percent (eo:cloud_cover). limit int None Largest number of products; when there are more, the most recent ones.

Returns a pandas.DataFrame sorted by datetime with the columns product (the name of the .SAFE), datetime (UTC), tile, cloud_cover (percent), baseline (processing baseline, "05.09") and platform. Earth Search has the Level 1C products from 2017 on.

df = zeit.find_l1c(tile="23LKC", start="2023-07-01", end="2023-07-31", max_cloud=30)
safe = zeit.download_l1c(df.iloc[0])

docs.title: download_l1c
docs.text:
zeit.download_l1c(product, dest=None, n_jobs=4)

Downloads a Sentinel-2 Level 1C product to a local .SAFE directory that level2 reads. The files come from the public bucket gcp-public-data-sentinel-2 of Google Cloud Storage (no credential; the assets of Earth Search point to another bucket, without MTD_MSIL1C.xml): only what level2 reads, the two XML files and the 13 band files (not the true-colour image), in the layout of the product. Each file goes to <name>.part and is renamed once its size and MD5 match the listing of the bucket; a file already there with the right MD5 is not downloaded again, so an interrupted download resumes. Transient errors are retried with a growing wait.

Parameter Type Default Description product str, row or DataFrame required The name of the .SAFE, or a row or a table of find_l1c (a table downloads all of them and gives the list). dest path None The folder that gets the .SAFE; by default the l1c cache (ZEIT_CACHE_DIR/l1c). n_jobs int 4 Simultaneous downloads; at most 8.

Returns the pathlib.Path of the .SAFE directory. Raises ValueError for a product the bucket does not have (the message names it) and RuntimeError for a file whose MD5 is not the listed one.

docs.title: download_dem
docs.text:
zeit.download_dem(area, dest=None, n_jobs=4)

A Copernicus GLO-30 DEM (30 m) covering a scene or a box, as one GeoTIFF in EPSG:4326: what level2(dem=) takes. The tiles come from the cop-dem-glo-30 collection of Earth Search (public COGs, read anonymously and only the windows that are needed) and are mosaicked in the geometry of the source, never resampled one by one onto the grid of the scene, so there is no seam. The area is the footprint of the scene (its UTM edges densified) plus 6 arc-seconds, because the bilinear warp reads neighbours. Where tiles of different resolution meet (the GLO-30 widens its cells in longitude beyond 50 degrees of latitude) the mosaic has the finest cell. Where there is no tile (the sea) the value is -32767, the no-data of level2.

Parameter Type Default Description area path or 4 numbers required A local .SAFE directory (the footprint of the scene) or (lon_min, lat_min, lon_max, lat_max) in degrees. dest path None A folder, or a .tif path; by default the dem cache (ZEIT_CACHE_DIR/dem). A file already there is reused. n_jobs int 4 Simultaneous reads of tiles; at most 8.

Returns the pathlib.Path of the GeoTIFF (float32). Raises ValueError for a scene that crosses the antimeridian (not handled) and for an area without any tile (all sea: use topography=False in level2).

docs.title: tmask
docs.text:
zeit.tmask(
    data, *, green="green", swir="swir1", scale=10000.0,
    nodata="auto", chunks=None,
)

Flags clouds and cloud shadows the QA band missed, from each pixel's time series (Tmask, Zhu & Woodcock 2014): a robust harmonic model (MATLAB's robustfit with Tukey's bisquare, as CCDC's own Tmask, in Rust, every pixel in parallel) is fitted to the green and SWIR bands of every pixel, and observations more than 0.04 (reflectance) above it in green (clouds) or below it in SWIR (shadows) are flagged. One function for a (time, band, y, x) cube in memory or dask, or anything load_raster reads; the dates come from its time coordinate. It replaces apply_tmask_stack and run_tmask_pixel (the per-pixel engine, still in zeit._tmask).

Parameter Type Default Description data DataArray or path required A (time, band, y, x) cube with green and SWIR bands, or one pixel: a (time, band) series (the result is (time)). green str or int "green" The green band, by name or position. swir str or int "swir1" The SWIR band (SWIR1, ~1.6 µm), by name or position. scale float 10000.0 Reflectance scale of the data (1.0 for reflectance in 0-1); the thresholds are in reflectance. nodata "auto", float or None "auto" Value marking a missing observation: the raster's NoData (0 for integer data without one), a number, or None. chunks "auto", dict None Inputs read from disk: None reads into memory; otherwise the result is lazy, computed block by block.

Returns clear (time, y, x), bool: True for a clear observation, False for a cloud, a shadow or no observation (NoData, NaN, or not above 0 in either band). Pixels with 5 or fewer valid dates are not screened. Georeferenced as the input.

cube = zeit.load_raster("landsat/", pattern=r"_(?P<date>\d{8})_(?P<band>\w+)\.tif$")   # (time, band, y, x)
clear = zeit.tmask(cube, green="green", swir="swir1")
cube = cube.where(clear)                         # clouds and shadows become NaN
qa = xr.where(clear, 0, 4)                       # or as CCDC's Fmask codes (0 clear, 4 cloud)

docs.title: parallax_clouds
docs.text:
zeit.parallax_clouds(
    cube, potential, *, variability=None, saturated=None, bright=None,
    bands=None, scale="auto", nodata="auto", return_cdi=False, n_jobs=-1,
)

Sentinel-2 clouds from the potential cloud pixels by the parallax test: FORCE's cloud_parallax (cloud-ll.c, FORCE 3.11, David Frantz, GPL-3.0-or-later; the method is Frantz, Haß, Uhl, Stoffels and Hill 2018, Remote Sensing of Environment 215:471-481). The detectors of the 10 m bands look at the ground one after the other, so a high object is seen at slightly different places in B07, B8A and B08, while a surface object (snow, a roof, bare soil) is at the same place in all of them. The ratio of red edge 3 to NIR (B07 / B8A) varies little at a cloud and the ratio of the broad NIR, smoothed by a 5 x 5 Gaussian kernel of sigma 0.5, to NIR (B08 / B8A) a lot; the Cloud Displacement Index is (var_x - var_y) / (var_x + var_y) of the two over 7 x 7 blocks of the 20 m grid (each block is 2 x 2 pixels of the 10 m one) and is close to -1 at a cloud. Blocks with a CDI of -0.5 or less, or below 0 where the minimum of the variability probability over the 15 x 15 blocks around is above 0.8, are cloud seeds if every block of their 3 x 3 neighbourhood qualifies (an erosion by one block); the clouds grow into the 8-connected blocks with a CDI in [-1, -0.25); each block goes back to four 10 m pixels; saturated pixels are added and every cloud pixel that is not bright is removed.

This is Frantz's own step. The rest of FORCE's cloud detection is derived from Zhu's Fmask and is not ported (Fmask's current repository, github.com/GERSL/Fmask, is MIT-licensed as of 2026-11-07, and none of its parts is used here): what cloud_parallax takes from it are inputs of this function, the potential cloud pixels (potential), the variability probability (variability), the bright pixels (bright) and the saturated ones (saturated). FORCE's clear-sky and clear-sky-land pixels and their counts, and the cloud cover, are passed to cloud_parallax but never read, and are not inputs.

Parameter Type Default Description cube DataArray required Reflectance (time, band, y, x) or (band, y, x) on the 10 m grid (20 m bands as four equal pixels, as for sentinel2_resmerge) with rededge3 (B07), nir (B08) and nir08 (B8A), or B07 B08 B8A; and blue green red unless bright is given, and swir16 (B11) too for the computed variability. In memory. potential boolean array required Broadcastable to (time, y, x): the potential cloud pixels (Fmask's, or from any cloud product). variability float array None Broadcastable to (time, y, x): Fmask's variability probability in [0, 1] (FORCE keeps it times 10000 as an int16, and so does Zeit: it is rounded to that). By default 1 - max(abs(NDVI), abs(NDSI), whiteness) of Zhu and Woodcock (2012, Remote Sensing of Environment 118:83-94), clipped to [0, 1]: NDVI = (B8A - red) / (B8A + red), NDSI = (green - SWIR1) / (green + SWIR1), the whiteness the sum over blue, green and red of the distance to their mean relative to the mean; a zero denominator gives an index of 0. Where saturated, a positive NDVI and a negative NDSI are set to 0, the paper's adjustment for pixels whose visible bands saturate (the paper gave it for Landsat 7; Sentinel-2's saturation is rare and flagged in its quality bands, which is where saturated comes from). saturated boolean array None Broadcastable to (time, y, x): saturated pixels, which are cloud if bright. By default none. bright boolean array None Broadcastable to (time, y, x). By default the mean of blue, green and red is above 0.15 (FORCE's 1500). bands dict None The cube's band of each role (rededge3 nir nir08 blue green red swir16), when its names are not the usual ones. scale "auto" or float "auto" What the reflectance is multiplied by in the data (10000 for integers or values above 2, else 1). The values are taken to FORCE's units (times 10000, as int16) for the computation. nodata "auto", float or None "auto" Missing values besides NaN: the raster's NoData (0 for an integer cube without one), a number or None. A pixel with a missing value in B07, B08 or B8A is FORCE's "off": never cloud. return_cdi bool False Also return the CDI. n_jobs int -1 Threads (the processors zeit may use by default).

Returns a boolean (time, y, x) (or (y, x)) DataArray, True for cloud, with the cube's coordinates; with return_cdi=True a tuple of it and the CDI (below).

pcp = potential_cloud_pixels(s2)        # Fmask's, or the cloud flag of a product
cloud = zeit.parallax_clouds(s2, pcp, saturated=saturated)
cloud = zeit.buffer_mask(cloud, 300)    # FORCE's CLOUD_BUFFER

Where it differs from FORCE. There is no force= switch: the values are FORCE's (short units, float and double where it has them, its order of summation) and its threads do not race, so there is nothing to choose. The one change is for odd sizes. FORCE steps through the image in twos and indexes the 20 m grid by i / 2, which writes outside the arrays when a side is odd (Sentinel-2 tiles are even); here the last row or column of an odd image is not part of any block and is never cloud (unless saturated and bright), while the smoothing still reads it. As in FORCE, a block whose first pixel is off is skipped even if the other three have data.

Agreement with FORCE. The cloud mask and the CDI (bit for bit) equal those of FORCE's cloud_parallax in every pixel and block on synthetic scenes with parallax-displaced clouds, built-up patches, off pixels, saturated and non-bright pixels (a C harness of FORCE's own functions; Against the Original Implementations).

docs.title: cloud_displacement_index
docs.text:
zeit.cloud_displacement_index(
    cube, *, potential=None, bands=None, scale="auto", nodata="auto", n_jobs=-1,
)

The Cloud Displacement Index of parallax_clouds on its own, float32 (time, y // 2, x // 2) (or (y // 2, x // 2)): on the 20 m half-resolution grid where it is computed (FORCE does not bring it back to 10 m, the clouds are), the coordinates those of the centres of the 2 x 2 blocks. A block has a CDI only if it has a potential cloud pixel and at least three blocks of the 7 x 7 around it have one, since the ratios of the others are left out of the variances; else it is NaN (FORCE's -9999). Near -1 at a cloud, around 0 or above for a bright surface. potential (broadcastable to (time, y, x)) is every pixel by default, which gives a CDI everywhere; the other parameters are those of parallax_clouds (the bands are rededge3, nir and nir08).

docs.title: buffer_mask
docs.text:
zeit.buffer_mask(
    mask, distance, *, units="m", resolution=None, force=False, n_jobs=-1,
)

Buffers the True pixels of a boolean mask: FORCE's cloud buffer (buffer_ of imagefuns-cl.c, which its Level 2 processing applies to the cloud, cirrus and shadow masks and the snow layer, CLOUD_BUFFER = 300 m by default). Every True pixel grows into the disc of the midpoint circle algorithm of integer radius r: the axis points at distance r are in, and so are (r, 1), a little fatter than the true disc (89 pixels for r = 5). With units="m", r = int(distance / resolution) as FORCE converts it (truncated; the resolution is the x spacing of a DataArray, or resolution=); with units="px" it is distance, a whole number. A radius of 0 changes nothing.

Parameter Type Default Description mask boolean DataArray or array required (y, x) or (time, y, x); each date is buffered on its own. distance float required The buffer, in units. units "m" or "px" "m" resolution float None The pixel size in metres, for units="m" when the mask is not a DataArray with an x coordinate. force bool False FORCE's behaviour at the borders (below). n_jobs int -1 Threads.

Returns a boolean mask as mask.

Where it differs from FORCE. FORCE's loop only buffers the pixels at least r from the borders and then replaces the mask by what was drawn, so a True pixel within r of an edge is lost and a cloud at the edge gets no buffer. force=True does that (and equals FORCE in every pixel); the default keeps every True pixel and draws its disc clipped at the edge, the same everywhere else. Zeit does not draw from every True pixel as FORCE does: each output row looks up the nearest source in the rows of the disc's runs, so the time hardly depends on how much is True (FORCE's takes seconds with a large cloud and a radius of 30).

docs.title: unmix
docs.text:
zeit.unmix(
    data, endmembers="souza2005", *, bands=None, sum_to_one=True,
    nonneg=True, scale="auto", ndfi=True, cloud_threshold=None,
    nodata="auto", chunks=None, n_jobs=-1,
)

The fraction of each endmember (pure material) in every pixel and date: a 30 m Landsat pixel of forest after selective logging is part canopy (green vegetation), part dead wood and litter (non-photosynthetic vegetation), part soil and part shade, and the fractions show the damage that the reflectance hides. The unmixing is fully constrained least squares (non-negative fractions that add up to one; Heinz & Chang 2001), in Rust, every pixel and date in parallel; the active set solves each pixel exactly. RStoolbox's mesma (R), whose NNLS iterates to a tolerance, takes 22 s on 1000 x 1000 pixels of 6 bands and 4 endmembers; Zeit 1.2 s on one thread, 0.13 s on 19, its residual never larger (benchmarks/vs_originals/unmix.py). Also exported as zeit.unmix.

Parameter Type Default Description data DataArray or path required Reflectance (time, band, y, x) or (band, y, x), in memory or dask. endmembers str, DataFrame or dict "souza2005" "souza2005": green vegetation (gv), shade, non-photosynthetic vegetation (npv), soil and cloud for Landsat's blue, green, red, NIR, SWIR1 and SWIR2 (Souza et al. 2005, with the cloud endmember of CODED, as CODED uses them). Or a table: rows endmembers, columns bands of the cube, reflectance 0–1 (or × 10000). bands list of str None The cube's band for each column of the endmembers, when the names differ (by default found by name: nir, B08, SR_B5...). sum_to_one, nonneg bool True, True Fractions adding up to one; fractions non-negative. scale "auto" or float "auto" What the reflectance is multiplied by: 10000 for integers or values above 2, else 1. ndfi bool True Also the NDFI (below), when the endmembers include gv, npv, soil and shade. cloud_threshold float None Mask observations whose cloud fraction is above this (CODED: 0.05). nodata, chunks, n_jobs "auto", None, -1 As elsewhere.

Returns an xarray.Dataset with one variable per endmember (its fraction), rmse (of the rebuilt spectrum, in reflectance) and ndfi, on the cube's dimensions but band, lazy if the cube is.

The NDFI (Normalized Difference Fraction Index; Souza et al. 2005) is (GVs − (NPV + soil)) / (GVs + NPV + soil), with GVs = GV / (1 − shade): near 1 in closed forest, lower where the canopy was damaged, below 0 on bare soil and pasture. It is also an index of compute_indices (compute_indices(cube, ["NDFI"])) and of the Earth Engine downloads.

fractions = zeit.unmix(landsat, cloud_threshold=0.05)
fractions.ndfi.zeit.plot()                       # page through the years

docs.title: smooth
docs.text:
zeit.smooth(
    data, *, method="whittaker", lmbda=10.0, weights=None, window=5,
    polyorder=2, nodata="auto", chunks=None, n_jobs=-1,
)

Smooths time series along time, keeping their dates, georeferencing and type. One function for every input: a cube (time, y, x) or (time, band, y, x) in memory or dask, anything load_raster reads, or one pixel's pandas.Series indexed by dates. It replaces apply_whittaker_filter and apply_savgol_filter.

  • Whittaker (default; Eilers 2003): a penalised least-squares curve that follows the data more or less closely (lmbda). The dates may be unevenly spaced: the penalty uses the time between them, measured in median steps of the series, so lmbda means the same on any spacing (on an even series it is the classic smoother). Missing observations (NaN, NoData) weigh 0 and are filled by the curve; weights down-weights hazy ones.
  • Savitzky-Golay (method="savgol"): a local polynomial over window dates, as scipy's savgol_filter, for evenly spaced series (regularise first with regularize_time_series). Missing observations are first interpolated linearly in time.
Parameter Type Default Description data DataArray, path or pd.Series required The series to smooth (see above). method str "whittaker" "whittaker" or "savgol". lmbda float 10.0 Whittaker: smoothness, larger is smoother (10 light for a 16-day NDVI series, 1000 strong). weights array or DataArray None Whittaker: a weight per observation, same shape as data (1 clear, 0.2 hazy, 0 cloudy; see qc_sentinel2_scl). window int 5 Savitzky-Golay: window length in dates (odd). polyorder int 2 Savitzky-Golay: order of the local polynomial. nodata "auto", float or None "auto" Value marking a missing observation: the raster's NoData (0 for integer data without one), a number, or None. chunks "auto", dict None Inputs read from disk: None reads into memory; otherwise the result is lazy. n_jobs int -1 Whittaker: threads. -1: all the cores but one, or every core of a cluster job (how they are counted).

Returns an xarray.DataArray with the same dims and coordinates (a pandas.Series for a Series). Floats keep their type; integer data with a NoData value (NDVI × 10000 in Int16) is rounded back to its type, NoData where a pixel has no observation at all; integer data without one comes back as float32. attrs["smoothing"] names the method, and zeit.plot(cube, fit=smoothed) draws the curve over a clicked pixel's series.

ndvi = zeit.load_raster("S2_ndvi_2022.tif")                    # (time, y, x), clouds as NaN
smooth = zeit.smooth(ndvi, lmbda=100)                          # gaps filled by the curve
weighted = zeit.smooth(ndvi, weights=zeit.qc_sentinel2_scl(scl))
sg = zeit.smooth(ndvi_16d, method="savgol", window=7)
zeit.plot(ndvi, fit=smooth)                                    # click a pixel: raw and smoothed

docs.title: desawtooth
docs.text:
zeit.desawtooth(values, stopat=0.9)

LandTrendr's spike removal for a single series: one-year spikes (up or down) are dampened toward their neighbours. landtrendr already applies it internally through its spike_threshold parameter, so call this only to inspect or pre-process series yourself.

Parameter Type Default Description values 1-D array required One pixel's series. stopat float 0.9 Each point gets a spike score (1 = a perfect one-year spike). Spikes are corrected strongest first while the strongest score exceeds stopat, so lower values correct more points. As in the original IDL code, the first correction is always applied. 
zeit.desawtooth(np.array([8000, 8100, 3000, 8050, 7900, 8000.0]))
# array([8000., 8034.7, 8025.2, 8050., 7900., 8000.])

docs.title: Interpolation and standardization
docs.text: Ported from the time series analysis of FORCE 3.11.00 (Frantz 2019, GPL-3.0-or-later): interpolate is its TSI, standardize its STANDARDIZE. The statistics, trends and clear-observation counts of the same chain are in FORCE time series analysis; the tutorial runs the whole chain, and Against the original implementations has the agreement with FORCE.

docs.title: interpolate
docs.text:
zeit.interpolate(
    data, method="rbf", *, step=16, start=None, end=None, times=None,
    sigma=(8, 16, 32), cutoff=0.95, window=16, modes=3, trend=True,
    fit=None, period=365.25, dates=None, band=None, nodata="auto",
    chunks=None, n_jobs=-1,
)

Interpolates every pixel's series to a regular grid of dates, or to any dates you give. One function for every input, like smooth: a (time, y, x) cube (in memory or dask), anything load_raster reads, a (time, band, y, x) cube or Dataset with band=, a numpy array with dates=, or one pixel's series. The dates are needed and must not decrease; NaN (and NoData) marks a missing observation. Ported from FORCE's TSA (Frantz 2019), with four methods:

  • RBF ("rbf", default; Schwieder et al. 2016): an ensemble of Gaussian kernels of standard deviations sigma (days), each cut where its mass reaches cutoff, weighted by how much data it finds around each date. The kernels are combined into one weight per integer day, the same average as FORCE's loop over kernels. A date with no valid observation within the largest kernel is NaN.
  • Linear ("linear"): straight lines between the valid observations on either side, constant beyond the first and last.
  • Moving average ("moving"): the mean of the valid observations within window days (closed).
  • Harmonic ("harmonic"; Zhu et al. 2015): an offset, an optional slope and up to 3 harmonics of period, fit by iteratively reweighted least squares with bisquare weights (tuning 4.685, MAD scale; the algorithm of GSL's gsl_multifit_robust). fit=(first, last) fits on part of the series and predicts the rest, which is FORCE's near-real-time mode.

The grid is FORCE's: from start (default the first date) every step days, floor((end - start + 1) / step) dates, end being the last date by default. No date is made after end.

Parameter Type Default Description data DataArray, path, ndarray or pd.Series required The series to interpolate (see above). method str "rbf" "rbf", "linear", "moving" or "harmonic". step int 16 Days between the dates of the grid. start, end date None First and last date of the grid. Default: the first and last date of the series. times list of dates None Any dates for the result, instead of the grid (start, end and step are then not allowed). sigma sequence of float (8, 16, 32) RBF: standard deviations of the kernels in days, increasing. cutoff float 0.95 RBF: the share of each kernel's mass kept (0-1). window float 16 Moving average: the half-width in days. modes int 3 Harmonic: the number of harmonics (1-3). trend bool True Harmonic: add an offset-and-slope term. fit (date, date) None Harmonic: the window the model is fit on (inclusive). Default: the whole series. period float 365.25 Harmonic: the period in days. dates list None Date of each time step, for inputs that carry none. band str or int None The index to use in a (time, band, y, x) cube or a Dataset. nodata "auto", float or None "auto" Value marking a missing observation besides NaN, as in smooth. chunks "auto", dict None Inputs read from disk: None reads into memory; otherwise the result is lazy. n_jobs int -1 Threads. -1: all the cores but one, or every core of a cluster job (how they are counted).

Returns an xarray.DataArray (time, y, x) with the new dates, the coordinates and georeferencing of the input, and attrs with the method and its parameters (a pandas.Series for a Series). Float32 for float32 input, else float64; the values are not rounded.

Differences from FORCE, all deliberate:

  • The output is float, not FORCE's int16: no rounding to the data's scale and no clipping.
  • The harmonic's period is 365.25 days, the real year; FORCE counts 365 on a calendar without leap days. The time is centered and scaled inside and the system solved by Cholesky on balanced columns, which does not change the fit.
  • A pixel whose harmonic IRLS cycles without converging (about 1 in 100 in the benchmark, found by the core) is left out of the comparison with FORCE: neither implementation settles on a fit, and a handful of them differ from FORCE by more than 1. A pixel with fewer valid observations in fit than coefficients is NaN.
ndvi = zeit.load_raster("S2_ndvi_2018_2022.tif")                   # (time, y, x), clouds as NaN
tsi = zeit.interpolate(ndvi, "rbf", step=16)                       # FORCE's default grid
daily = zeit.interpolate(ndvi, "linear", times=pd.date_range("2020", "2021", freq="D"))
nrt = zeit.interpolate(ndvi, "harmonic", fit=("2018-01-01", "2020-12-31"), end="2022-12-31")

docs.title: standardize
docs.text:
zeit.standardize(
    data, method="normalize", *, ddof=1, dim=None, dates=None,
    band=None, nodata="auto", chunks=None, n_jobs=-1,
)

Standardizes every pixel's series along an axis (FORCE's STANDARDIZE and STANDARDIZE_FOLD). The mean and the deviation are those of the valid observations; missing observations stay NaN. Takes the same inputs as interpolate (the dates are not needed), and any axis through dim=, such as the year of temporal_metrics(..., by="year").

Parameter Type Default Description data DataArray, path, ndarray or pd.Series required The series to standardize. method str "normalize" "normalize": (x - mean) / std, the z-score; "center": x - mean. ddof int 1 Degrees of freedom of the deviation (n - ddof; 1 is the sample deviation, as FORCE). dim str None The axis to standardize along: "time" (default when it exists) or another, such as "year". A metric axis of length 1 is dropped; with more, choose one with .sel(metric=...). dates list None Date of each time step, for inputs that carry none (not needed for the result). band str or int None The index to use in a (time, band, y, x) cube or a Dataset. nodata "auto", float or None "auto" Value marking a missing observation besides NaN. chunks "auto", dict None Inputs read from disk: None reads into memory; otherwise the result is lazy. n_jobs int -1 Threads. -1: all the cores but one, or every core of a cluster job (how they are counted).

Returns the cube with the same dims, coordinates and georeferencing (a pandas.Series for a Series). A series with fewer than 2 valid observations is left as it is; a constant series gives NaN when normalized. Float32 for float32 input, else float64, not rounded as FORCE's int16 is.

z = zeit.standardize(tsi)                                          # z-score of each pixel along time
anomaly = zeit.standardize(tsi, "center")                          # x - mean
yearly = zeit.temporal_metrics(ndvi, ["mean"], by="year")
zy = zeit.standardize(yearly, dim="year")                          # each year against the others
